precepts.text: I am the Lord thy God, which have brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage. Egypt is the house of bondage, the house of slavery, the house of captivity. Egypt and slavery are synonymous.
precepts.point: And no man shall buy you. Because the first time Moses saved us. Before that we had Samson save us, we had Gideon. The Lord said this slavery, nobody. Only my son can do it. Only I will do it. Christ said, I will come down there and save you. No one else can do that. No Nat Turner will do it. No Gabriel Prosser will do it. No Toussaint Louverture will do it. No Dessalines will do it. No Nanny of the Maroons will do it. No Medgar Evers will do it. No Martin will do it. No Malcolm will do it. I will do it. That is what God is saying there.

note.label: Foundational Babylonian Advocates: Division Among the Dispersion

precepts.why:
“And the Lord shall bring thee into Egypt again with ships”. The Lord will bring you into captivity again, because Egypt represents bondage. What does Egypt represent? The first commandment tells you.

“I am the Lord thy God, which have brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.”

Egypt is the house of bondage: the house of slavery, the house of captivity. Egypt and slavery are synonymous. So when the curse says into Egypt again, it means into slavery again.

And it says with ships. Not imaginary ships, not planes, not trains, not a blimp or a hot air balloon: with ships. Ships will be used during this Egypt. And the Lord says it is “by the way whereof I spake unto thee, Thou shalt see it no more again”: that Egypt as a nation, the one we walked into the first time, we will never see again as slaves. That is done. This Egypt is by boats, and “there ye shall be sold unto your enemies for bondmen and bondwomen”, slave men and slave women, sold from those ships to the same enemies who put a yoke of iron upon our neck in verse 48.

Last of all, “and no man shall buy you”. The first time, the Lord brought us out of the house of bondage by Moses, and before that we had Samson and Gideon save us. This slavery, nobody. No Nat Turner, no Gabriel Prosser, no Toussaint Louverture, no Dessalines, no Nanny of the Maroons, no Medgar Evers, no Martin, no Malcolm. Only the Lord will do it, through his son. Christ said, I will come down there and save you.

precepts.text: And thy heaven that is over thy head shall be brass, and the earth that is under thee shall be iron. The Lord shall make the rain of thy land powder and dust. That is what it looks like when the rain does not come.
precepts.point: When we harvest crops we look forward to the rain coming. We needed the rain to come. When it did not rain, we knew the Lord was not dealing with us. That is how he punished us. We read that in Deuteronomy 28. So the blessing the Lord will give us will be in the application of his laws.

note.label: God's People Need Charity, Healing & Trust

precepts.why:
Hosea ends with a promise: “he shall come unto us as the rain, as the latter and former rain unto the earth.” What is the analogy of the former and latter rain? It's going to be a blessing. When we harvested crops, we looked forward to the rain coming. We needed the rain to come. When it didn't rain, we knew the Lord wasn't dealing with us. That's how he punished us.

We read that in Deuteronomy 28: “And thy heaven that is over thy head shall be brass, and the earth that is under thee shall be iron. The Lord shall make the rain of thy land powder and dust: from heaven shall it come down upon thee, until thou be destroyed.” That is what it looks like when the rain does not come: the heaven shut like brass, the ground hard as iron, and powder and dust in place of rain.

So when Hosea says the Lord will come unto us as the rain, it is the curse being lifted. “Come, and let us return unto the Lord: for he hath torn, and he will heal us”. We were torn by captivity and slavery, and he will heal us, meaning redeem us out of this situation. After two days, two thousand years, he revives us, and in the third day he raises us up to who we are, to our identity.

“Then shall we know, if we follow on to know the Lord”: if we follow on to apply what God tells us to do, then shall we be bound up and healed. The rain the Lord withheld in the curses comes back as a blessing, and that blessing will be in the application of his laws.

precepts.text: Under these wood gods like Christianity, the old wooden cross; there's many denominations under Islam; and our people are scattered everywhere in those false religions, even in Judaism.
precepts.point: I will set up shepherds over them, which shall feed them, and they shall fear no more, neither shall they be lacking. Cuz right now we are lacking as a race, as a people. We're lacking knowledge, wisdom, and understanding. But when you break it down, we're lacking rulership. We are lacking dominion of the earth. We're lacking our own country, a fortified family, a nation. We're lacking everything. We are a lacking people.

note.label: Living Your Life As A Hireling

precepts.why:
“Woe be unto the pastors that destroy and scatter the sheep of my pasture! saith the Lord.” Jeremiah 23 really talks about the essence of hirelings. How do they scatter the sheep? In Christianity they scatter them into the Baptist church, the Catholic church, the holiness church, whatever denomination. We are being divided rather than united as the twelve tribes of Israel. Even in the time of Christ there were the Sadducees, the Pharisees, the Stoics, the Epicureans and the Herodians; we were being scattered then, and it's happening today.

Moses said where it would lead: “And the Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other; and there thou shalt serve other gods, which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone.” Under these wood gods, like Christianity with the old wooden cross, and the many denominations under Islam, our people are scattered everywhere in those false religions, even in Judaism.

Remember, this is about Israelites; it is not so much talking about Esau. “Ye have scattered my flock, and driven them away”: driven them away from the truth that they are the Israelites of the twelve tribes. But the Lord says “I will gather the remnant of my flock out of all countries whither I have driven them”.

precepts.text: The Lord shall bring a nation against thee from far, from the end of the earth, as swift as the eagle flieth: that's Rome, when they came in and destroyed us and ran us out of Jerusalem, in Luke 21 and Matthew 24:15, the abomination of desolation. A nation whose tongue thou shalt not understand: we did not understand their tongue when they landed. A nation of fierce countenance, which shall not regard the person of the old, nor shew favour to the young: they ain't care about old or young; they enslaved everybody. Until he have destroyed thee: we are a destroyed people today. Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies, and he shall put a yoke of iron upon thy neck.
precepts.point: And the earth helped the woman, and the earth opened her mouth, and swallowed up the flood. The earth that's helping the woman is this Bible. This Bible is helping us understand what happened to us, what's happening to us right now, and what's going to happen to us in the future.

note.label: Awake and Return: Overcoming Babylon's Hypnosis

precepts.why:
“And to the woman were given two wings of a great eagle”. Who is the eagle? The eagle was Rome at the time, and Rome is an extension of this place called America. Moses tells us about that eagle: “The Lord shall bring a nation against thee from far, from the end of the earth, as swift as the eagle flieth”. That's Rome, when they came in and attacked us in Luke 21, the abomination of desolation of Matthew 24:15, when they destroyed us and ran us out of Jerusalem. From the end of the earth: from Europe.

“a nation whose tongue thou shalt not understand”: we did not understand their tongue when they landed here. Columbus found the Taino, a people who shared food, land and knowledge and fed him as an honored guest, and he wrote that they would make fine servants, and with fifty men he could make them do whatever he wanted. They knew what they came for. Within fifty years the Taino nation was virtually extinct. In Africa they sent explorers, missionaries with Bibles and the cross, and traders with gifts first; they ate at the tables of kings while mapping the gold and rubber, got treaties signed in crafty, ambiguous words, and at the Berlin conference of 1884 sat around a table and split up the continent. They came as swift as the eagle flieth. You can never trust that red man, that devil, that dragon.

“A nation of fierce countenance, which shall not regard the person of the old, nor shew favour to the young”: they didn't care about old or young; they put everybody to death and enslaved everybody. “And he shall eat the fruit of thy cattle, and the fruit of thy land, until thou be destroyed”, and leave neither “corn, wine, or oil, or the increase of thy kine”, kine being cattle, “until he have destroyed thee.”

Then the woman is nourished in her place, and that is America, where we've been nourished through their welfare system, their disability system, their politics, their religions, their educational and economic system. “Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies which the Lord shall send against thee, in hunger, and in thirst, and in nakedness, and in want of all things”. Hungry, thirsty, needing clothing, a passport, a visa, a death certificate, anything we need, we have to go to them. “and he shall put a yoke of iron upon thy neck, until he have destroyed thee.” The red man put a yoke of iron upon our necks, and we are destroyed today as a people. Even the ones speaking up for us say we love America: that is how destroyed we are.

precepts.text: The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God. Not the whole world: the Israelites are the children of God. The Bible bears witness with our spirit that we are them children.
precepts.point: And they shall be upon thee for a sign and for a wonder, and upon thy seed for ever. The curses is the sign: if our spirit resonates with the signs in Deuteronomy 28:15-68 and Genesis 49, we going to realize that we are the Israelites. And for a wonder: we're supposed to be wondering how the greatest people on earth got so low. It's going to be upon our seed until Christ's return.

note.label: Awake and Return: Overcoming Babylon's Hypnosis

precepts.why:
“Moreover all these curses shall come upon thee, and shall pursue thee, and overtake thee, till thou be destroyed”. I don't care what country you are in, what state, what continent: these curses are following us. That's why we're getting shot down in the streets and killed left and right; the Most High has to do something to wake us back up. We are a destroyed nation, and we haven't understood that yet.

“And they shall be upon thee for a sign and for a wonder”. The curses are the sign. That is how we know we are the Israelites: the Bible gives us the signs to look out for, in Deuteronomy 28:15-68 and in Genesis 49, and if our spirit resonates with those signs, we are going to realize that we are the Israelites.

That is Romans 8:16: “The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit, that we are the children of God”. That we, the Israelites, are the children of God. Not the whole world. The spirit itself, the Bible, bears witness with our spirit that we are those children.

And “for a wonder”: we are supposed to be wondering what happened. We are the greatest people on earth; how did we get so low? It will be upon our seed for ever, upon our children until Christ's return. Brothers want to argue the trinity while our people are being killed, holding the name Israel and refusing everything that goes with it. The sign is on us, and the spirit bears witness with ours: we are Israel, and we have to come back to the Lord.

precepts.text: Now if you know you got to serve this man for food, water, and clothing, you can't go I hate your guts, I just want to. You think you're going to have a job? You're going to lose everything.
precepts.point: I met this one brother years ago at camp Eastern Parkway. He's on medication. He said, I would join you, but I have psychosis; I can't work, I get violent. I said, why? He says, I hate white people. He said, when I sit in the office or if I'm doing construction, I'll look at them and I just want to harm them.

note.label: Drowning in Sin & Perdition

precepts.why:
“Thou shalt not abhor an Edomite; for he is thy brother”. Use this verse to your advantage; don't run from it. In Romans 9:13 Paul speaks on behalf of God, and that is what God says about Esau. But God's law to us is: thou shalt not abhor an Edomite, for he is thy brother, a wicked brother.

And look at our condition: “Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies which the Lord shall send against thee, in hunger, and in thirst, and in nakedness, and in want of all things”. If you know you have to serve this man for food, water and clothing, you can't go around saying I hate your guts, I just want to harm you. You think you're going to have a job? You're going to lose everything.

There was a brother at camp on Eastern Parkway, on medication, who said he couldn't work because he gets violent: I hate white people; when I sit in the office or do construction, I look at them and I just want to harm them. And there was a martial artist, a black belt, who drew young Haitian brothers to him, skinny at first and diesel two or three months later, calling themselves the barbershop crew in Brooklyn. One night a brother called to be gotten out of jail: they were getting diesel and learning to fight to do home invasions and burglaries.

The bottom line is, professing yourself to be an Israelite is not on the premise of wanting to harm white people. A lot of Israelite camps teach that, and the leaders of those camps are bums: either they are bums or they live off the congregation, and they can talk that way without repercussions because they have no boss to answer to. We serve our enemies under the curse, so we keep the law: we do not abhor the Edomite.

precepts.text: Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies, in hunger, and in thirst, and in nakedness, and in want of all things. We wanted food, clothing, housing, shelter, and we also got that old time religion from them too.
precepts.point: They are the most needy of any people in our country, the book said. It does say needy, and the Bible says it too.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
The third direction to the masters: serve your necessities by your slaves so as to prefer God's interest and their spiritual and everlasting happiness; teach them the way to heaven. So in want of all things we wanted food, clothing, housing, shelter, and we also got that old time religion from them too.

“Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies which the Lord shall send against thee, in hunger, and in thirst, and in nakedness, and in want of all things”. In want of all things: even our religion had to come from the enemy we were serving.

The next page shows what that religion was for. They wrote that we were redeemed with them by Christ from the slavery of Satan and may live with them in the liberty of the saints in glory. They want us to go to heaven with them and live with them. That's called hell. That mind was beaten into us: a brother on the street asked if the Edomite could be saved, and said if he goes to hell, so will I, because he doesn't want to go anywhere without his master. That is the want of all things the curse brought, and why the master's reading of Colossians 3:22 still holds our people.

precepts.text: They came out as a whirlwind to scatter me: their rejoicing was as to devour the poor secretly. When Christ returns, these same people who had us in slavery will try to fight against him. And the devouring is secret: after the emancipation proclamation came the traps that still oppress us to this day.
precepts.point: Video played from a 1966 CBS documentary, Black Power, White Backlash, filmed in Cicero, Illinois, where 15,000 black people worked in the factories every day but not a single black family could live: residents said they would be afraid to go out at night, that you really could not trust any of them, and one said there are many good coloreds, but the ones that are going to march I don't like. They do not like when we march, because when we march we have our pride, our dignity, and our confidence. They do not like when we stand up as the nation of Israel; it angers them and it makes them afraid.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
Officer Tatum was asked if black men like him were better off during slavery, and he answered, 100 percent. He said that after slavery there was an explosion of success, black Wall Street, men married to the women they had children with, and now look at the inner cities. What he does not understand is that he thinks white people just switched and started loving us after they let us out of slavery.

“Thou didst strike through with his staves the head of his villages: they came out as a whirlwind to scatter me”. When Christ returns, these same people who had us in slavery, and have us in slavery, are going to try to fight against Christ.

“their rejoicing was as to devour the poor secretly.” These same slave owners rejoice to devour the poor, and they do it secretly. Even though slavery supposedly ended with the emancipation proclamation in 1863, then what? You had the school to prison pipeline. Redlining. Sundown towns. Sharecropping. It is still the same thing.

Look at us now, and why? Because he is setting up all these traps. That is why he is still oppressing us to this day, and that is the “yoke of iron upon thy neck, until he have destroyed thee.” But Tatum cannot see that.

They do not like when we stand up as the nation of Israel; it angers them and it makes them afraid.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
Habakkuk said their rejoicing is “to devour the poor secretly.” Who are the poor? “What shall one then answer the messengers of the nation? That the Lord hath founded Zion, and the poor of his people shall trust in it.”

The poor of his people. We are the poor that they are devouring secretly. The poor are Israel, and it is Zion that the Lord founded for them to trust in.

Tatum blames the murders, the violent crime and the abortions in the inner cities on our people alone. But who legalized abortion? The white people. Who started Planned Parenthood with Margaret Sanger? He just skips past that; according to him they are not the cause. That is the secret devouring of the poor, and it is the yoke of iron of Deuteronomy 28:48 still on our neck.

precepts.text: Herein do I exercise myself, to have always a conscience void of offence toward God, and toward men. What is better than standing up for God and standing up for his people? precepts.why:
Tatum said black people need to do better: y’all whole life is activism, y’all still complaining and protesting like y’all still slaves. Why were the brothers in Ocean Springs, Mississippi? Because one of our brothers, Nolan Wells, had a mysterious death with a bunch of white people around it, in a town known for lynching black people. Yes, we are activists. Yes, we stand up for righteousness and speak against the evils and atrocities that happen to our people. That puts fear in our oppressors, and he is doing their bidding: hey, you’ve been cooning great lately.

So what is better than standing up for God and standing up for his people? “And herein do I exercise myself, to have always a conscience void of offence toward God, and toward men.”

We always have to do what is right toward God and toward our people. Better looks like getting your household in order, not committing fornication and adultery, taking care of your family. What is better than that? That is what a conscience void of offence looks like, and he is not speaking from the point of a black man.

precepts.text: Thou deliveredst them into the hand of their enemies, who vexed them: and in the time of their trouble, when they cried unto thee, thou heardest them from heaven, and thou gavest them saviours, who saved them out of the hand of their enemies. That is what is happening now: the Lord is starting to hear our cry, and the saviors are going city to city and country to country teaching the word of God.

precepts.why:
“Therefore thou deliveredst them into the hand of their enemies, who vexed them”. That is what happened to us: we have been delivered into the hands of our enemies, the yoke of iron of Deuteronomy 28:48.

“and in the time of their trouble, when they cried unto thee, thou heardest them from heaven”. That is what is happening now. The Lord is starting to hear our cry. We are supposed to pray unto the Lord until he brings vengeance; that is what the Bible tells us to do.

“and according to thy manifold mercies thou gavest them saviours, who saved them out of the hand of their enemies.” How is that happening? By the purple and gold going to this city and that city, this country and that country, teaching the word of God. These are the saviours, and the saviours showed up in Ocean Springs, Mississippi.

So when we see these things happen to our people, yes, we are going to be there, and no, we are not going to stop. We don’t care if we have coons among our own people; we are going to rise up and save the day, because that is how God ordained it. Tatum is mad about it. Get mad. You hate your people and you hate your God.

precepts.why:
A 1966 CBS documentary, Black Power, White Backlash, went into Cicero, Illinois, where 15,000 black people worked in the factories every day but not a single black family lived, and every one of them had to leave when the sun went down. A resident said there are many good coloreds, but the ones that are going to march, I don’t like.

They do not like it when we march, because when we march we have our pride, our dignity, our respect and our confidence. They do not like when we stand up as the nation of Israel; it angers them and it makes them afraid. We have been marching; Marcus Garvey was marching back in the day.

“But Pharaoh shall not hearken unto you, that I may lay my hand upon Egypt, and bring forth mine armies, and my people the children of Israel, out of the land of Egypt by great judgments.” Mine armies. We have been marching since Egypt, and we marched around the walls of Jericho.

Israel came out of Egypt as the armies of the Lord, by great judgments on the ones who held them. That is why our marching troubles our oppressors.

precepts.why:
They do not like when we stand up on our feet with confidence as the nation of Israel, not as blacks, but as the nation of Israel.

“And after three days and an half the Spirit of life from God entered into them, and they stood upon their feet; and great fear fell upon them which saw them.”

Great fear falls on them when they see us rise up as the children of God, as the army of the living God. That is what the man in Cicero feared when he said he could not stand the ones who march, and it is what puts fear in our oppressors when the brothers show up in a town like Ocean Springs. The yoke of iron destroyed us, but the Spirit of life from God stands us back on our feet.

We go to our people just like the forefathers did, and we bring the Bible with us. We do not just go to one city or one state; wherever our people are scattered and afflicted, we are there.

precepts.why:
Tatum claimed he had not seen black Hebrew Israelites going out and saying anything in the community when a black man died. That is a lie; he has been found a liar. That is what we do literally every week. We teach in the hoods and the ghettos where our people are: O Block in Chicago, East St. Louis, Memphis, Miami, Compton, LA, Philly. We go toe to toe and face our people.

“And they taught in Judah, and had the book of the law of the Lord with them, and went about throughout all the cities of Judah, and taught the people.”

They taught in Judah: we go to our people just like the forefathers did. They had the book of the law of the Lord with them: we bring the Bible with us. They went throughout all the cities: we do not just go to one city or one state. Wherever our people are scattered, wherever our people are being afflicted, we are there, teaching the people.

precepts.why:
A pastor named Pam declared that the gospel cannot be for one ethnicity only, that it cannot be just for black men or for white men, and that this is a heretical doctrine preached by false, cultic ministries. Either the cultic ministries are right or Jesus is right; somebody is wrong. It’s you, Pam.

“But he answered and said, I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.”

It is only for one nation, twelve tribes. If you are not part of that, you are not getting in. Some of our people are bugged the hell out, and it is a direct correlation to slavery. A white pastor even said God blessed black Americans through white people and slavery, and Tatum agrees with that. But Christ was sent to the lost sheep of the house of Israel, the same people under the yoke of iron of Deuteronomy 28:48.

precepts.why:
The holy city “had a wall great and high, and had twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel”.

Praises to the Most High for that. The kingdom is only for God’s people. The gates of the city carry the names of the twelve tribes, and no other nation’s name is written there.

That settles what Pam called heresy. Christ was not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel, and the city he brings has twelve gates for the twelve tribes. The same people the Lord sent into bondage with a yoke of iron upon their neck are the people whose names are on the gates.

precepts.text: Because thou servedst not the Lord thy God with joyfulness and with gladness of heart for the abundance of all things. We are not happy to keep the Most High's holy days; we show joyfulness and gladness of heart to celebrate pagan holidays instead, but for Passover, the Sabbath, the day of atonement, and the feast of unleavened bread, the beautiful holy days the Lord gave us, we are mad. Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies in hunger, and in thirst, and in nakedness, and in want of all things: for everything you need, food, water, clothing, hospital care, you have to go to the same enemy, because we broke God's law. And he shall put a yoke of iron upon thy neck, until he have destroyed thee: until you are dead bodies in the street of America, not even knowing who you are, celebrating the Fourth of July when your people were in slavery on that same date. Jeremiah 23 says woe be unto the pastors that destroy and scatter the sheep of my pasture; the preachers that deceived our people with his Bible will answer for it.
precepts.point: Where she is nourished from the face of the serpent. Who is feeding us in this captivity? The serpent, the same power the scripture identifies as the dragon. That is why we go to Deuteronomy 28.

note.label: 250 Years of Celebration 400 Years of Sweat Equity (Pt 2)

precepts.why:
“And to the woman were given two wings of a great eagle, that she might fly into the wilderness”: a great escape out of Jerusalem when Rome came against us, into Africa, the same place Joseph took Mary and the child to hide from Herod. Verse 6 says the same: “the woman fled into the wilderness, where she hath a place prepared of God, that they should feed her there”. She is nourished “for a time, and times, and half a time, from the face of the serpent.” Who is feeding us from the face of the serpent? The white man is the devil the Bible speaks of. Deuteronomy 28 shows crystal clear who this demon is that's feeding us.

First, why: “Because thou servedst not the Lord thy God with joyfulness, and with gladness of heart, for the abundance of all things”. It lines up with Luke: these be the days of vengeance, because we broke the commandments of the Lord. We ain't happy to keep the Most High's high holy days. We show joyfulness and gladness of heart for the Fourth of July and these pagan, evil, wicked holidays; but when it comes to Passover, the Sabbath, the day of atonement, the feast of unleavened bread, the beautiful holy days the Lord gave you, you got your lips stuck out. You mad.

“Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies which the Lord shall send against thee, in hunger, and in thirst, and in nakedness, and in want of all things”. God did that. That is how we're fed: for food, for water, for clothing, even the textiles they stole, for hospital care, for anything you need, you have to go to the same enemy. We don't own nothing. God set it up that way because we made our father mad.

“and he shall put a yoke of iron upon thy neck, until he have destroyed thee.” Who put the yoke of iron on our neck? The so-called white man, the serpent of Revelation. The same serpent put a chain around your neck, until you are dead bodies in the street of America, not even knowing who you are, your mind destroyed, celebrating the Fourth of July when your people were in slavery on that same date.

And the evil preachers who deceived us will pay too. Jeremiah 23: woe be unto the pastors that destroy and scatter the sheep of my pasture. Taking his Bible and lying to God's people with it is a serious crime. So the woman nourished from the face of the serpent is Israel in this captivity, fed by the enemy the Lord sent against us for not serving him with gladness.

precepts.text: And thou shalt be only oppressed and spoiled evermore. That is what Elihu was talking about.
precepts.point: By reason of the multitude of oppressions they make the oppressed to cry: they cry out by reason of the arm of the mighty. This was Elihu speaking to Job prophetically about times to come. Are we not oppressed today?

note.label: Job Sees America's 250th Anniversary

precepts.why:
Elihu tells Job: “By reason of the multitude of oppressions they make the oppressed to cry: they cry out by reason of the arm of the mighty.” This was Elihu speaking to Job prophetically about times to come. Are we not oppressed today? Yes.

Moses wrote the same thing in the curses: “And thou shalt grope at noonday, as the blind gropeth in darkness, and thou shalt not prosper in thy ways: and thou shalt be only oppressed and spoiled evermore”. That is what Elihu was talking about. The oppressed crying out by reason of the arm of the mighty is Israel under the curses, oppressed and spoiled evermore.

Solomon said it too: “So I returned, and considered all the oppressions that are done under the sun: and behold the tears of such as were oppressed, and they had no comforter; and on the side of their oppressors there was power”. They have the guns, the nuclear weapons, the court system; they have it all, and we have nothing. That is the arm of the mighty.

But the Most High “looked down from the height of his sanctuary” to “hear the groaning of the prisoner; to loose those that are appointed to death”. We are the prisoner: sons of God in a weak body, ruled and dominated by a wicked race of people and subject to their laws. We groan waiting for “the redemption of our body”. We want our godhood back, rulership back, dominion back, to reign on this planet like we once did.

precepts.text: And I am very sore displeased with the heathen that are at ease: for I was but a little displeased, and they helped forward the affliction. God was a little displeased with us, and they afflicted us more and more.
precepts.point: And no man shall buy you: no man shall redeem us from the curses. There is only one redeemer, brothers and sisters, and that is Christ.

note.label: Job Sees America's 250th Anniversary

precepts.why:
Moses said “thy life shall hang in doubt before thee”. When we got emancipated we thought we were free. Juneteenth. Then the white man took the sheet out of the closet, cut two holes in it, put on the white robe, and it was time for the KKK, patterned after the capirotes of Spain from the Inquisition. Spain was in this country, and what they had over there they brought here. As soon as we thought we were free, they gave us hell.

The Most High speaks to that in Zechariah: “And I am very sore displeased with the heathen that are at ease: for I was but a little displeased, and they helped forward the affliction.” God was a little displeased with us, because we broke his laws and his commandments. But the heathen afflicted us more and more and more. That is what God is saying right there.

Then back to Moses: “thou shalt fear day and night, and shalt have none assurance of thy life”. Imagine building your own town because white folks don't want you drinking their water or going to their school: your own cab company, your own hospital, your own bank. Then you hear a noise, and they are dropping dynamite on the city from planes and murdering a lot of us. That is the heathen helping forward the affliction, far beyond the little displeasure God had with us.

So the curses of Deuteronomy 28 came on us for our sins, but the nations went further than God sent them, and he is very sore displeased with them for it. The heathen that are at ease today are the ones who will answer for what they added to our affliction.

precepts.text: The Lord shall smite thee with madness, and blindness, and astonishment of heart. Some of our young men are mentally deranged under the curses, and the music glorifies it.
precepts.point: And thou hast laid thy body as the ground: our people will weep publicly for men who never said or did anything for them, but will not cry for each other. That is Isaiah 51:23 in action.

note.label: Job Sees America's 250th Anniversary

precepts.why:
Isaiah says “Thy sons have fainted, they lie at the head of all the streets, as a wild bull in a net”. That is why our young men hang on the corners: uncontrollable, like wild bulls in a net. It's a trap; this system is a trap. “they are full of the fury of the Lord”. What is the fury of the Lord? Deuteronomy 28:15-68, the curses God put upon us, and they are on our young men.

Even this one: “The Lord shall smite thee with madness, and blindness, and astonishment of heart”. Some of our young men are mentally deranged. The ones doing that new type of singing, drill: they are murderers, they are killers, and they don't care.

It is seen in the neighborhood. A house in Queens, a playground across the street with about twenty adorable little kids running around. Time went by, those little kids grew up, and they were having shootouts, bullets flying through the house, the kids and the wife thrown on the floor. That is what they turned into.

So the sons fainted at the head of all the streets are the sons of Israel under the curse of madness. They are full of the fury of the Lord, the rebuke of thy God, and that is why they cannot be controlled.

precepts.text: The Lord shall smite thee with madness, and blindness, and astonishment of heart. Our people do things with no rhyme or reason. That is being smitten with madness; we have generational curses.
precepts.point: None calleth for justice, nor any pleadeth for truth. You might say our people are always in the street crying no justice, no peace. But the justice our people want is money. They do not want the justice of the Bible. Many of the families of our unjustly slain, we may march with them and support them, but you never see the internal change; they are still celebrating the holidays of the very system they are angry at. They want truth regarding their case, but they do not want God's truth as a whole.

note.label: The Negro Community: A Wasteland of Tears

precepts.why:
“For your hands are defiled with blood, and your fingers with iniquity.” Our hands in the black and brown community are defiled with blood. In Joliet a young man, twenty-three years old, shot to death his own mother, his aunt, his uncle, his bedridden brother and his three sisters, killed another man and shot one more, and then shot himself. That's trauma right there, and the law explains it: “The Lord shall smite thee with madness, and blindness, and astonishment of heart.”

The Lord shall smite thee with madness: meaning our people are insane. No rhyme, no reason to what they do or why they do it. That's being smitten with madness. We have generational curses. Three teens on a thirty-hour spree of armed robberies and the murder of a churchgoing man; a woman charged with stabbing and killing a three-year-old boy, appearing in court laughing and smiling: that is stricken with madness.

The Bible says, thou shalt not kill, and we are not taught that in church, so some of us grow up with a hateful and murderous spirit on us. No matter how bad, insulting or degrading these videos are, they are filtered through the Bible, showing the stage and state of where we are today, and it is still proof that we are the children of Israel under the curses. The Bible ain't the white man's book. The Bible is our book.

That is why the Lord's hand is not shortened and his ear is not heavy, and still he does not save: “your iniquities have separated between you and your God.”

precepts.text: And thou shalt grope at noonday, as the blind gropeth in darkness, and thou shalt not prosper in thy ways: and thou shalt be only oppressed and spoiled evermore, and no man shall save thee. Isaiah 59 is this curse in real time.
precepts.point: And judgment is turned away backward, and justice standeth afar off: for truth is fallen in the street, and equity cannot enter. And he that departeth from evil maketh himself a prey: when you repent and come to this truth, everybody around you starts hating you. And the Lord saw it, and it displeased him that there was no judgment.

note.label: The Negro Community: A Wasteland of Tears

precepts.why:
“We grope for the wall like the blind, and we grope as if we had no eyes: we stumble at noonday as in the night; we are in desolate places as dead men.” We got eyes, but we act like we ain't got none. We act like what we just saw didn't happen. The curse said it would be so: “And thou shalt grope at noonday, as the blind gropeth in darkness, and thou shalt not prosper in thy ways: and thou shalt be only oppressed and spoiled evermore, and no man shall save thee.”

We are like blind people, but we have eyes. We see we're not prospering as a people. We see we're under constant oppression as a people. But we act like we don't see it, because oppression has become so normal to us; it's our everyday life.

It's high noon, but in our minds we are so spiritually blind it is like night for us. “we are in desolate places as dead men”: that's the black and brown community, desolate places, our people like the walking dead. Isaiah 59 is Deuteronomy 28:29 in real time.

That is why verse 9 says, “Therefore is judgment far from us, neither doth justice overtake us.” We want to live filthy lives, evil lives, violent lives, and then expect justice from God. It don't work like that. Oppressed and spoiled evermore, and no man shall save thee.

precepts.text: And the Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other. We were scattered everywhere, and that includes, as we are finding out, China and Japan.
precepts.point: French art book of Nanban screens: black slaves in the Japanese paintings of the 1500s, carrying loads, rowing the boats, carrying the litters on their shoulders, the same thing we had to do for the white folks over here. Why are these books not in English in America? We had to go to foreign countries to dig this up, because they keep it secret.

note.label: The Madmen Of China And Their Hatred For Black People

precepts.why:
“And the Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other; and there thou shalt serve other gods, which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone.”

We were scattered everywhere, and that includes, as we are finding out, China and Japan. The paintings from Japan in the 1400s and 1500s show the black faces, and the black faces are slaves, brought over by the Portuguese and Spanish. In ancient China the Kunlun, African slaves, were given as tribute gifts during the Tang dynasty, and slavery peaked under the Tang and Song dynasties. The Portuguese brought enslaved Africans to Macau in large numbers in the 1500s, where they formed the core of its defense and defeated the Dutch in the Battle of Macau in 1622.

You don't learn this in school, and you definitely ain't going to learn it in Sunday school. They keep it secret and hidden. We thought these people were our friends; they had us as slaves too. That is why no nation wants to give us reparations: all nations got to pay.

This is how Israel came to be among all people from one end of the earth to the other, and why the question stands: “Hath Israel no sons? hath he no heir?” The Lord answers that Israel shall be heir again.

precepts.text: The reason Isaiah 11 says he shall set up an ensign for the nations is because we were going to be scattered among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other, and live as Gentiles.
precepts.point: The majority of the masses did not have what we call the Old Testament. It was the learned men that had the parchments, and it was their job to instruct the people. But now God gave it to the apostles to teach.

note.label: Acts 10 Reloaded: Call No Man Common

precepts.why:
Isaiah 11 says “he shall set up an ensign for the nations”. Why for the nations? Because Israel was going to be scattered: “And the Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other; and there thou shalt serve other gods, which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone.”

We were going to be scattered in all these nations and live as Gentiles, serving other gods. So the ensign set up for the nations is set up to “assemble the outcasts of Israel, and gather together the dispersed of Judah from the four corners of the earth.” The ones he gathers out of the nations are Israel.

That is what the Jews meant in John 7 when they asked, “will he go unto the dispersed among the Gentiles”? They knew the curse: Israel scattered from one end of the earth to the other.

precepts.text: Thy sons and thy daughters shall be given unto another people. That could have happened at any moment: your son ripped out of your arms and sold, and you will never see your children again, and there shall be no might in thine hand. A bottle of whiskey would not stop that. They did not have that. They had to endure this thing sober, knowing the Lord is still going to be with us somehow, so I cannot off myself, because a generation is going to come from me.
precepts.point: And thy life shall hang in doubt before thee: in chattel slavery our lives were in doubt every day. Every day there was a chance we would be killed.

note.label: The Developmental Psychology of Being Hated

precepts.why:
“And thy life shall hang in doubt before thee”: in chattel slavery our lives were in doubt every day. Every day there was a chance we would be killed, a chance we might get lynched. And not only the lives of the mothers and fathers were in doubt; our sons were in doubt too. That is why verse 32 is read here: “Thy sons and thy daughters shall be given unto another people.”

That could have happened at any moment, any day. Your son ripped out of your arms to be sold to Master so-and-so, and you would never see your children again. From the day that child was born until the day someone said, I want that one as a slave, the parents lived with it, and they had nothing to say about it. “and thine eyes shall look, and fail with longing for them all the day long”: they watched their sons get taken away and watched their daughters get taken away. That is the failing of eyes and the sorrow of mind of verse 65: no way to change your reality, no future you can see for your children.

“and there shall be no might in thine hand”: no might in our hands to stop it. And there was no alcohol for them. A bottle of whiskey would not have stopped that. They had to endure this thing sober, knowing the Lord was still going to be with us somehow, some way. So they could not off themselves, because a generation was going to come from them, from the wife and from the husband, and our seed would continue while they went through trauma after trauma.

It took faith to make it from morning to night and night to morning, and they did not even have the truth the way we know it today. They pushed through all that evil and ugliness so that you and I could sit here today. So what excuse do we have? We cannot leave our post to drink and get high, or put our head inside a bottle and a crack pipe, when our forefathers endured this and kept pushing.

precepts.text: I said, I would scatter them into corners, I would make the remembrance of them to cease from among men. The remembrance of who we are has ceased from amongst men. We didn't just forget; the nations made war with us and used crafty counsel: make sure them slaves cannot read and write. Ask a man today who the Israelites are and he points at the synagogue of Satan. Yet in Africa today there are millions professing they are the Israelites; just in Nigeria there is an Israelite community of millions, and they always knew.
precepts.point: The curses shall be upon thee for a sign, and for a wonder, and upon thy seed for ever. Why a sign? Like a McDonald's sign lets you know a McDonald's is there. Because according to prophecy we would be scattered in slavery and forget our nationality, God said: these curses are going to follow you and your seed, so no matter where you are scattered, when you read the Bible you're going to say, wait, this is talking about my people. In the future, Judah will need to identify who Israel is; today you identify the Israelites by the curses.

note.label: Judgement! To Hell with Your Reparations!

precepts.why:
“And they shall be upon thee for a sign and for a wonder, and upon thy seed for ever.” Why a sign? When you see a McDonald's sign, it lets you know a McDonald's is there. The curses have to be upon us for a sign because we would be cut off from our heritage, and in the future Judah will need to identify who Israel is. How do you identify the Israelites today? By the curses.

Deuteronomy 32:26 shows why: “I said, I would scatter them into corners, I would make the remembrance of them to cease from among men”. We were scattered into corners in slavery, and the remembrance of who we are, our nationality, all of it, has ceased from among men. We did not just forget because time went on. We forgot because the nations made war with us and took crafty counsel: make sure those slaves cannot read and write. They destroyed us as a people and took our nationality. Ask a Chinese man today who the Israelites are, and he points at the fake people in the land, the synagogue of Satan.

Yet go to Africa today and you will see millions of people professing that they are the people of God, the Israelites, though you will not see it on the news. Just in Nigeria there is a large Israelite community of millions. Over generations of misinterpretation and mixing customs with the Hamitic tribes they do not keep the laws the way they are supposed to, but they always knew they were Israel.

So God did it real nice. Esau would take our nationality from us, but the curses would follow us and our seed, so that no matter where we are scattered, in Africa, America, South America, China, Iran, the islands, when we read the Bible we say: wait, this is talking about my people.

precepts.text: The joy of the Lord is your strength: coming back to serve the Lord, we have to serve him with gladness, because we did not have gladness before and that is why we went into captivity.
precepts.point: Even the understanding you have of the Bible was taught to you by Esau. That is why you do not have the right spirit on you.

note.label: I Come In Peace

precepts.why:
“Because thou servedst not the Lord thy God with joyfulness, and with gladness of heart, for the abundance of all things”. We had the whole earth, the whole thing belonged to us, and we were ungrateful children. We murmured and murmured and murmured. The Lord delivered us out of Egypt, we watched plagues upon plagues come upon Egypt, and then we turned back and worshipped the same gods the Lord destroyed in Egypt.

Even today it is like pulling teeth to get many of us to be happy and joyous on a feast day. We have to change that, because we did not have gladness before, and that is why we went into captivity. So now, coming back to serve the Lord, if you want your strength, you had better apply Nehemiah: “the joy of the Lord is your strength.” There are no two ways about it.

The blueprint is already set. The Bible tells you exactly what you need to do and how you need to go about living; we just do not want to listen. The curse of serving our enemies came because we would not serve the Lord with gladness, and the way back is to serve him with the joy that is our strength.

precepts.text: Once you serve another Jesus, you get another gospel, and once you get another gospel you receive another spirit. That is the spirit in these churches.
precepts.point: Even the understanding you have of the Bible was taught to you by Esau. That is why you do not have the right spirit on you.

note.label: I Come In Peace

precepts.why:
“Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies”, “in want of all things”. We serve for food, for water, for clothes, for all kinds of paperwork, because nothing is real in your life until the so-called white man says it is real. You are not even dead until the white man says you are dead; without a paper stamped by Esau Edom you cannot even get the money your daddy left behind.

So even the understanding you have of the Bible was taught to you by Esau, and that is why you do not have the right spirit on you. When you read 2 Corinthians 11:4, once you serve “another Jesus”, you get “another gospel”, and once you get the other gospel, you get “another spirit”. That is the spirit in these churches; that is why those little boys are twitching in the church.

The enemy did not only put the yoke on our necks; he set up shop in our heads using Christianity, and you have to be dumb to believe Jesus is white with no Bible proof while you carry the biggest Bible under your arm. The only way for us to deal right is to come out of these churches and join this movement. No weapons, no guns, no physical fight will save us; the only thing that will save us is this book.

precepts.text: Once you serve another god, the Lord gives you up unto vile affections. Look at what is coming out of the churches now. You keep staying in that Christianity, serving a false deity, do not be surprised when the evil spirit jumps on you and you start defiling your body.
precepts.point: Even the understanding you have of the Bible was taught to you by Esau. That is why you do not have the right spirit on you.

note.label: I Come In Peace

precepts.why:
Look at the Christian church: gangsters, homos and lesbians coming out of that church. It has mutated to a whole different level. Why? Because once you serve another God, according to the book of Romans, the Lord gives you up unto “vile affections”.

So if you keep staying in that Christianity, serving the false deity, or keep being a Muslim, serving a rock, do not be mad when the evil spirit jumps on you and you start defiling your body, changing kind and doing all kinds of nonsense. That is what is going to happen. Your choir master is making all those songs dedicated to another deity, and the Lord is unhappy with that. He says, you want to devote all your time to serving another god? I am going to remove myself from here, and watch what happens to you.

That is the curse of Deuteronomy 28:47-48 working in the spirit: because we did not serve the Lord with gladness, he sent our enemies against us, and when we took up their gods, he gave us up. Thank the Lord for saving a remnant, because we all would have been as Sodom and Gomorrah.

precepts.text: Fear ye not, stand still, and see the salvation of the Lord: for the Egyptians whom ye have seen to day, ye shall see them again no more for ever. The scripture already said we would never see those Egyptians again; so the Egypt of Deuteronomy 28:68 cannot be ancient Egypt.
precepts.point: The definition of Egypt, from the Hebrew Mizraim, was read in class: shut in, restraint, misery, tribulation, distress. So when Moses says you will go into Egypt again with ships, it means we would go into a place of captivity, misery, and tribulation, and we would be carried there on ships.

note.label: Passover Class: Exodus From America Modern Day Egypt

precepts.why:
Deuteronomy 28:68 says “the Lord shall bring thee into Egypt again with ships, by the way whereof I spake unto thee, Thou shalt see it no more again”. Moses is being very specific, and Exodus 14:13 explains it. At the Red Sea he told the people: “Fear ye not, stand still, and see the salvation of the Lord, which he will shew to you to day: for the Egyptians whom ye have seen to day, ye shall see them again no more for ever.”

The scripture already said we would never see those Egyptians again, for ever. So when Moses says we will go into Egypt a second time, the Egypt he is speaking of cannot be ancient Egypt. The people would have said, Egypt again? We are going back to Egypt a second time? And he explains: I am not talking about the Egypt you just came out of. The way whereof I speak unto thee, thou shalt see it no more again. It is a different Egypt.

And this time we go into it with ships. Moses saw the end. The Lord showed him the Israelites thrown on cargo slave ships and brought here to America: the transatlantic slave trade. Egypt, from the Hebrew Mizraim, means shut in, restraint, misery, tribulation, distress. So going into Egypt again means going into captivity, misery and tribulation again, carried there on ships, sold to our enemies for bondmen and bondwomen. That is why Revelation 11:8 calls the great city, Mystery Babylon, America, spiritually Egypt.

precepts.text: Moreover he will bring upon thee all the diseases of Egypt, which thou wast afraid of; and they shall cleave unto thee. The diseases of Egypt themselves are named among the curses.
precepts.point: Thou shalt grope at noonday, as the blind gropeth in darkness: and thou shalt not prosper in thy ways: and thou shalt be only oppressed and spoiled evermore. As a nation of people we do not prosper in our ways; we are only oppressed and spoiled evermore.

note.label: Passover Class: Exodus From America Modern Day Egypt

precepts.why:
Deuteronomy 28:15 says that if we will not hearken unto the voice of the Lord to do all his commandments and his statutes, “all these curses shall come upon thee, and overtake thee”. Verse 27 names one of them: “The Lord will smite thee with the botch of Egypt”. Then verse 60: “Moreover he will bring upon thee all the diseases of Egypt, which thou wast afraid of; and they shall cleave unto thee.”

That is what we need to see. The curses of Deuteronomy 28 did not just come out of nowhere. A lot of them are the same curses that were on us in ancient Egypt: the botch of Egypt, the diseases of Egypt, the oppression of Egypt. God said in Exodus 3:9, “I have also seen the oppression wherewith the Egyptians oppress them.” Our forefathers were oppressed in ancient Egypt, and they were oppressed here in America, and are still being oppressed here. The oppression is real.

So when the scripture calls America spiritually Egypt, it is because the same things that happened to us in ancient Egypt happened to us here, and the curses show it. The diseases of Egypt cleave unto us in this land, along with the rest: we grope at noonday, we do not prosper in our ways, and as a nation of people we are only oppressed and spoiled evermore.
