precepts.text: Israel did not serve the Lord with joyfulness for the abundance of all things.
precepts.point: God showed his word and statutes to Jacob and has not dealt so with any other nation.

note.label: Transforming from Immorality into Beautiful Civility Part 2

precepts.why:
“Because thou servedst not the Lord thy God with joyfulness, and with gladness of heart, for the abundance of all things”. The Lord gave us the abundance of all things, and we did not want to serve him for it. So he caused us to serve our enemies, and that is why we ended up falling underneath these people. That is not where our position is supposed to be.

Before we went into captivity we were celebrating the gods of the nations, and the Lord had a problem with that. Psalms 96:5 is his message and warning to us: “For all the gods of the nations are idols: but the Lord made the heavens.” Our God made everything; that is the God we are connected with. So-called Christmas, Thanksgiving and so-called New Year's are pagan, evil hella days, not holy days. How can you talk about Thanksgiving on stolen land?

We are not the nations. “He sheweth his word unto Jacob, his statutes and his judgments unto Israel.” “He hath not dealt so with any nation”. Our customs are his statutes and judgments; we have the Bible, not idols. And Jeremiah 10 says, “Hear ye the word which the Lord speaketh unto you, O house of Israel”, “Learn not the way of the heathen, and be not dismayed at the signs of heaven; for the heathen are dismayed at them.” Astrology, witchcraft and voodoo are the nations' problem, not ours. The Israelites are a special people, set above the nations, the jewels of God, and you have to see yourselves that way.

“For the customs of the people are vain”, void of anything credible: “one cutteth a tree out of the forest”, and “They deck it with silver and with gold”. That was the custom in the Babylonian empire, four empires before Christ was born in the time of Rome. What do lights, tin and silver on a tree have to do with Christ? Nothing. It is Sol Invictus, the unconquered sun, sun worship commemorating Nimrod, Tammuz, whom the women wept for in Ezekiel 8, celebrated on December 25th. Our people know Christ has nothing to do with it, the same way the Bible gives no white Jesus, but they will not stand up for truth.

Serving the gods of the nations instead of serving the Lord with gladness is what put us under our enemies. Anybody who continues to celebrate that madness now knows better and will be judged by the Most High.

precepts.text: Thou shalt beget sons and daughters, but they shall go into captivity.
precepts.point: For breaking the release, God proclaimed a liberty to the sword, the pestilence and the famine.

note.label: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.why:
“Thou shalt beget sons and daughters, but thou shalt not enjoy them; for they shall go into captivity.” That is slavery. It is a different thing from the servant of Leviticus 25, a poor Hebrew brother who sold himself to his brother for six years and went out free and furnished in the year of release. Christianity used the words servants, obey your masters, to make us think the Bible's servant was chattel slavery; it is not. Deuteronomy 28:41 is the captivity that came as the curse.

It is what Jeremiah 34 brought on us. Zedekiah made all the people covenant to let every Hebrew manservant and maidservant go free, “that none should serve himself of them, to wit, of a Jew his brother.” They obeyed, “But afterward they turned, and caused the servants and the handmaids, whom they had let go free, to return”. This is some negro stuff: the elites among us, those who had money, wanted to keep our own people in continuous servitude. So the Lord proclaimed a liberty for us “to the sword, to the pestilence, and to the famine”, to be “removed into all the kingdoms of the earth.” That is Deuteronomy 28. Babylon had just left, and God brought them right back. That is the result of hating our brothers and not loving our neighbour as ourselves. Even after Persia set us free, in Nehemiah 5 the nobles did the same thing again.

After the Persian captivity came the Greek. 1 Maccabees 3:41: “the merchants of the country, hearing the fame of them, took silver and gold very much, with servants, and came into the camp to buy the children of Israel for slaves”, and “a power also of Syria and of the land of the Philistines joined themselves unto them.” We look at the slave auction and think it is the first time this ever happened. No, the Greeks did this too, and other nations helped them.

2 Maccabees 5 shows it: Jason, an Israelite, a treasonous negro, “slew his own citizens without mercy”, treating his countrymen like enemies to please the Greeks, and he died cast out, with none to mourn him. “But he that doeth wrong shall receive for the wrong which he hath done” (Colossians 3:25). Then the king took the city: “fourscore thousand, whereof forty thousand were slain in the conflict; and no fewer sold than slain.” Apollonius was sent “to slay all those that were in their best age, and to sell the women and the younger sort”. The best age, the movers and shakers who make a nation thrive; take them and leave the old and feeble, and you destroy the nation, the same complaint made about the colonialists.

So the sons and daughters we begat went into captivity, sold by the Greeks, and after them by Rome, whose foothold came when Pompey captured Jerusalem in 65 BC, and the slave markets were full of black Jewish slaves. That is where breaking the year of release led.

precepts.text: The fruit of thy land and all thy labours shall a nation eat, and thou shalt be only oppressed and crushed alway.
precepts.point: This is prophecy for the northern kingdom in the Americas.

note.label: Babylon Speaks Plainly: Venezuela and the Real WMD

precepts.why:
“The fruit of thy land, and all thy labours, shall a nation which thou knowest not eat up; and thou shalt be only oppressed and crushed alway”. We are reaping what we have sown, especially the northern kingdom. Hosea 9 says we went a whoring from our God: we sought after the other nations and their ideals and made deals with them, and so “Ephraim shall return to Egypt, and they shall eat unclean things in Assyria.” That is servitude, dependence, and our resources consumed by others.

The oil, the land, the assets: everything the nations say we stole from them is really the fruit of our land, eaten up by a nation we knew not. Others eat our labour. That is what the whole documentary The End of Poverty is about.

The other nations are the ministers of evil unto us for the evil that we have done. Just as there is prophecy for Babylon that great city, there is prophecy for us, and this is it: oppressed and crushed alway, in Venezuela, Cuba, and all through Latin America.

precepts.text: Thou shalt serve thine enemies in hunger, thirst, nakedness and want of all things.
precepts.point: This is prophecy for the northern kingdom in the Americas.

note.label: Babylon Speaks Plainly: Venezuela and the Real WMD

precepts.why:
“Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies which the Lord shall send against thee, in hunger, and in thirst, and in nakedness, and in want of all things: and he shall put a yoke of iron upon thy neck, until he have destroyed thee.” This is for the northern kingdom especially. Our breakdown of it has often been very United States based, but when you go to these other countries you have to give the sense this way, because the people there are fully aware of the robbing of their resources.

Why these things in particular, hunger, thirst, nakedness and want of all things? Ecclesiasticus (Sirach) 39:26 names the chief things of life: “The principal things for the whole use of man’s life are water, fire, iron, and salt, flour of wheat, honey, milk, and the blood of the grape, and oil, and clothing.” When you target those things you dehumanize a people, taking away what is needful for them to live dignified. That is why they will never let the resources in their backyard be controlled by the people who own them, here or in Africa. “All these things are for good to the godly: so to the sinners they are turned into evil.” Because we have not repented of what Hosea 9 describes, we will not reclaim them until the Redeemer comes; in the meantime we must repent and keep the laws, statutes and commandments.

Sirach 34:21 shows it is violence: “The bread of the needy is their life: he that defraudeth him thereof is a man of blood.” You think violence has to be a sword, a bomb or a bullet, but “he that defraudeth the labourer of his hire is a bloodshedder.” The man in the documentary worked all day and still had nothing to go home to eat.

Lamentations 5 is the same picture: “Our inheritance is turned to strangers, our houses to aliens.” “We have drunken our water for money; our wood is sold unto us.” You see it now in Cuba, in Venezuela, in parts of Africa. “We have given the hand to the Egyptians, and to the Assyrians, to be satisfied with bread”, just as Hosea 9 says: we have given the power and sovereignty of our resources to Babylon the Great, the United States, and other nations, and China is working its way into Latin America. “Our fathers have sinned, and are not; and we have borne their iniquities.” With the Monroe Doctrine, the Roosevelt Corollary and the big stick, the northern kingdom is still paying for the sins of the forefathers. “Servants have ruled over us: there is none that doth deliver us out of their hand.”

Chains do not have to be chains anymore; this is economic slavery, and that is why Deuteronomy 28:48 is so profound. Baruch 3:8: “we are yet this day in our captivity”, “to be subject to payments, according to all the iniquities of our fathers, which departed from the Lord our God.” That is the key. We need this compassion to reach in and touch our people's souls. Babylon is speaking plainly; so must we.

precepts.text: Scattered among all people, there shalt thou serve other gods, wood and stone; that is how the Sabbath was forgotten.
precepts.point: Look up the blue laws, also known as Sunday laws; they help give understanding of why the Bible says remember the Sabbath day.

note.label: Exodus 20: The Ten Commandments

precepts.why:
“And the Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other; and there thou shalt serve other gods, which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone.”

Scattered among all people, Israel served other gods, wood and stone, gods neither they nor their fathers had known. That is how the Sabbath was forgotten: the people were forced into the religions of their captors. Look up the blue laws, also known as Sunday laws; they help give understanding of why the Bible says remember the Sabbath day.

precepts.text: Ye shall be sold unto your enemies for bondmen and bondwomen, and no man shall buy you; buy is interchangeable with redeem, and no nation redeemed Israel out of this captivity.
precepts.point: Redeem and buy are interchangeable words here: his kin come to redeem it meaning to buy it back. This is the prime example to reference for the curse that says no man shall buy you: no man shall redeem you. The other nations never came to say, we want to redeem Israel out of slavery and set them back to freedom; Israel has been in slavery for hundreds of years and no nation did that.

note.label: Leviticus 25: The Sabbath of the Land and the Year of Jubile

precepts.why:
“If thy brother be waxen poor, and hath sold away some of his possession, and if any of his kin come to redeem it, then shall he redeem that which his brother sold.” Redeem and buy are interchangeable words here: his kin come to redeem it, meaning to buy it back.

This is the prime example to reference for the curse: “there ye shall be sold unto your enemies for bondmen and bondwomen, and no man shall buy you.” No man shall buy you means no man shall redeem you.

The other nations never came to say, we want to redeem Israel out of slavery and set them back to freedom. Israel has been in slavery for hundreds of years and no nation did that. The kinsman redeemer of Leviticus 25 never came for us; that is the curse fulfilled.

precepts.text: If thou shalt hearken diligently unto the voice of the Lord, all these blessings shall come on thee and overtake thee; the same covenant of blessing and curse.
precepts.point: If Israel kept the commandments there would be no famine: rain in due season, the crops continually growing, the harvest coming in on time, and rain in the land even in a drought.

note.label: Leviticus 26: The Blessings and the Curses

precepts.why:
The blessings for walking in the statutes and keeping the commandments are the same blessings and curses read in Deuteronomy the 28th chapter. It is one covenant of blessing and curse.

Moses said, “if thou shalt hearken diligently unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe and to do all his commandments”, then “the Lord thy God will set thee on high above all nations of the earth: And all these blessings shall come on thee, and overtake thee, if thou shalt hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God.”

Rain in due season and the land yielding her increase is the first of those blessings. If Israel kept the commandments there would be no famine: the crops continually growing, the harvest coming in on time, and rain in the land even in a drought.

precepts.text: The enemy shall besiege thee in all thy gates, and thou shalt eat the fruit of thine own body, the flesh of thy sons and daughters, in the siege and straitness.
precepts.point: Eating the flesh of sons and daughters goes into 70 AD, and it also happened in the days of the kings when the city was besieged and there was such famine that a woman's son was boiled and eaten.

note.label: Leviticus 26: The Blessings and the Curses

precepts.why:
Deuteronomy gives the same curse and names the way it comes: by siege. The enemy “shall besiege thee in all thy gates, until thy high and fenced walls come down, wherein thou trustedst, throughout all thy land”.

“And thou shalt eat the fruit of thine own body, the flesh of thy sons and of thy daughters, which the Lord thy God hath given thee, in the siege, and in the straitness, wherewith thine enemies shall distress thee”. The enemies distress them, but it is the Most High walking contrary in fury, using the enemies to do it.

That is how it played out in the siege of Samaria, when the woman boiled her son, and again in 70 AD at Jerusalem.

precepts.text: Among these nations shalt thou find no ease, but a trembling heart, and failing of eyes, and sorrow of mind, fearing day and night with no assurance of life.
precepts.point: And ye shall perish among the heathen: many of us die in this land and in all the lands where we are scattered, and the land of the enemies eats the people up in oppression.

note.label: Leviticus 26: The Blessings and the Curses

precepts.why:
The faintness sent into the hearts of them that are left alive, in the lands of their enemies, is the same curse Deuteronomy 28 describes for the land of the enemies: “among these nations shalt thou find no ease, neither shall the sole of thy foot have rest: but the Lord shall give thee there a trembling heart, and failing of eyes, and sorrow of mind”.

And “thy life shall hang in doubt before thee; and thou shalt fear day and night, and shalt have none assurance of thy life: In the morning thou shalt say, Would God it were even! and at even thou shalt say, Would God it were morning!” That is the heart the sound of a shaken leaf chases.

Falling one upon another as it were before a sword when none pursueth is still seen to this day: even at these protests, when the rubber bullets, the tear gas, the water hoses, and the dogs come out, the people stumble and fall over one another trying to get away. And ye shall perish among the heathen: many of us die in this land and in all the lands where we are scattered, and the land of the enemies eats the people up in oppression.

precepts.text: The Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other, and there thou shalt serve other gods, wood and stone; the same prophecy in the curses.
precepts.point: And there ye shall serve gods, the work of men's hands, wood and stone: the wood is the cross of christianity and the stone is the kaaba stone at Mecca. Israel would fall into the heathen religions, christianity and islam, in the lands of the scattering.

note.label: Deuteronomy 4: Neither Add nor Diminish

precepts.why:
The same prophecy stands in the curses: “And the Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other; and there thou shalt serve other gods, which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone.”

Deuteronomy 4:27 is future prophecy of the scattering to the four corners of the earth, “ye shall be left few in number among the heathen”. And in those lands “ye shall serve gods, the work of men’s hands, wood and stone”. The wood is the cross of christianity and the stone is the kaaba stone at Mecca, gods which neither Israel nor their fathers had known. Israel would fall into the heathen religions, christianity and islam, in the lands of the scattering.

precepts.text: The Lord shall open his good treasure, the heaven to give the rain unto thy land in his season; thou shalt lend unto many nations and shalt not borrow.
precepts.point: This is the blessing side that Deuteronomy 28 spells out: when Israel kept the commandments, the Lord gave rain in due season in Israel's own land. Chapter 28 comes up in the reading in a few days; these are the basic precepts for it.

note.label: Deuteronomy 11: Remember His Acts, Keep His Commandments

precepts.why:
This is the blessing side that Deuteronomy 28 spells out. “The Lord shall open unto thee his good treasure, the heaven to give the rain unto thy land in his season, and to bless all the work of thine hand”. That is the same rain as here: “the rain of your land in his due season, the first rain and the latter rain, that thou mayest gather in thy corn, and thy wine, and thine oil.” When Israel hearkened diligently to the commandments, loving the Lord and serving him with all their heart and with all their soul, the Lord gave rain in due season in Israel's own land.

The blessing goes further than rain: “the Lord shall make thee plenteous in goods, in the fruit of thy body, and in the fruit of thy cattle, and in the fruit of thy ground, in the land which the Lord sware unto thy fathers to give thee”, and “thou shalt lend unto many nations, and thou shalt not borrow.” Corn, wine, oil, and grass in the fields for the cattle, that thou mayest eat and be full: it all hangs on hearkening to the commandments. Chapter 28 comes up in the reading in a few days; these are the basic precepts for it.

precepts.text: Thy heaven shall be brass and the earth iron; the Lord shall make the rain of thy land powder and dust, until thou be destroyed.
precepts.point: The things written aforetime were written for our learning: Jeremiah shows this curse landing in Israel's history, the ground chapt because there was no rain, and the confession that our backslidings are many.

note.label: Deuteronomy 11: Remember His Acts, Keep His Commandments

precepts.why:
The second part is the curse. If the heart is deceived and Israel turns aside to serve other gods, “the Lord’s wrath be kindled against you, and he shut up the heaven, that there be no rain, and that the land yield not her fruit”. Deuteronomy 28 spells out what a shut heaven is: “And thy heaven that is over thy head shall be brass, and the earth that is under thee shall be iron. The Lord shall make the rain of thy land powder and dust: from heaven shall it come down upon thee, until thou be destroyed.”

A heaven of brass gives no rain, and an earth of iron yields no fruit. No rain means drought: the crops cannot grow, and with no grass the animals have nothing to feed on, so the cattle go lean and there is no meat to eat. What comes down from heaven instead of rain is powder and dust, until thou be destroyed; that is how ye “perish quickly from off the good land which the Lord giveth you.”

precepts.text: The blessings of obedience that run through Deuteronomy 28:1-14: hearken diligently and all these blessings shall come on thee and overtake thee.
precepts.point: The blessing is what Deuteronomy 28:1-14 describes; the curse is what came upon Israel, running through Deuteronomy 28 to verse 68.

note.label: Deuteronomy 11: Remember His Acts, Keep His Commandments

precepts.why:
Moses sets before Israel “a blessing and a curse”. The blessing is what Deuteronomy 28:1-14 describes, and it opens this way: “And it shall come to pass, if thou shalt hearken diligently unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe and to do all his commandments which I command thee this day, that the Lord thy God will set thee on high above all nations of the earth: And all these blessings shall come on thee, and overtake thee, if thou shalt hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God.”

That is the blessing “if ye obey the commandments of the Lord your God”: set on high above all nations of the earth, with blessings that come on thee and overtake thee. Hearken diligently and observe to do all his commandments; the blessings run from verse 1 through verse 14 on that one condition.

precepts.text: The end of the curses that came upon Israel for not obeying: brought into Egypt again with ships and sold unto their enemies.
precepts.point: The blessing is what Deuteronomy 28:1-14 describes; the curse is what came upon Israel, running through Deuteronomy 28 to verse 68.

note.label: Deuteronomy 11: Remember His Acts, Keep His Commandments

precepts.why:
The curse is what came upon Israel, running through Deuteronomy 28 to verse 68, and this is its end: “And the Lord shall bring thee into Egypt again with ships, by the way whereof I spake unto thee, Thou shalt see it no more again: and there ye shall be sold unto your enemies for bondmen and bondwomen, and no man shall buy you.”

That is the curse “if ye will not obey the commandments of the Lord your God, but turn aside out of the way which I command you this day, to go after other gods”. Israel did turn aside, and the curses came all the way to the end: brought into Egypt again with ships and sold unto their enemies for bondmen and bondwomen. Blessing and curse were both set before Israel this day; the curse is the one our history shows.

precepts.text: The Lord shall open unto thee his good treasure, and thou shalt lend unto many nations and shalt not borrow; the blessing Israel forfeited by breaking the commandments.
precepts.point: This is the blessing that was to come upon us. Since we broke the commandments of the Most High, the other nations lend to us and we borrow from them; we go to them for loans and everything else.

note.label: Deuteronomy 15: The Year of Release and the Hebrew Servant

precepts.why:
The promise of verse 6 stands among the blessings of chapter 28: “The Lord shall open unto thee his good treasure, the heaven to give the rain unto thy land in his season, and to bless all the work of thine hand: and thou shalt lend unto many nations, and thou shalt not borrow.”

This is the blessing that was to come upon us, “Only if thou carefully hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe to do all these commandments”: lending to many nations and borrowing from none, reigning over many nations and none reigning over us.

Since we broke the commandments of the Most High, the other nations lend to us and we borrow from them; we go to them for loans and everything else. That is the blessing Israel forfeited by breaking the commandments.

precepts.text: Thou shalt lend unto many nations and shalt not borrow, and the Lord shall make thee the head and not the tail.
precepts.point: The same law was already read in Exodus: if thou lend money to any of my people that is poor by thee, thou shalt not be to him as an usurer.

note.label: Deuteronomy 23: Who May Enter the Congregation and the Holy Camp

precepts.why:
“Unto a stranger thou mayest lend upon usury; but unto thy brother thou shalt not lend upon usury”. Chapter 28 shows the blessing that lending to the stranger belongs to: “thou shalt lend unto many nations, and thou shalt not borrow. And the Lord shall make thee the head, and not the tail; and thou shalt be above only, and thou shalt not be beneath; if that thou hearken unto the commandments of the Lord thy God”.

That is our rightful place on the earth when we keep these commandments: the head and not the tail, lending to the nations and not borrowing. We should lend unto them and may take usury upon what we lend to them; but we should not do that to our own people. Usury is interest, and we are not to charge interest to each other when we loan each other anything.

precepts.text: The people of thy holiness have possessed it but a little while; our adversaries have trodden down thy sanctuary.
precepts.point: Isaiah sums up Deuteronomy 28:1-14: we possessed it but a little while. Israel had the blessings to a point when they went into the land, but only about eighty years at the full level, under David and Solomon. How Solomon abounded in gold, ships, and plenty of food you can read in 1 Kings.

note.label: Deuteronomy 28: The Blessings and the Curses That Identify Israel

precepts.why:
Deuteronomy 28:1-14 is the blessings: the enemies that rise up against thee shall “flee before thee seven ways”; the blessing is commanded “in thy storehouses, and in all that thou settest thine hand unto”; the Most High establishes thee an holy people unto himself; all people of the earth see “that thou art called by the name of the Lord” and are afraid of thee; thou shalt lend unto many nations and not borrow; thou shalt be “the head, and not the tail”, above only and not beneath. All of it hangs on one condition: “if that thou hearken unto the commandments of the Lord thy God”, and turn not aside after other gods.

Isaiah sums up what became of it: “The people of thy holiness have possessed it but a little while: our adversaries have trodden down thy sanctuary.” Israel had the blessings to a point when they went into the land, but only about eighty years at the full level, under David and Solomon. How Solomon abounded in gold, ships and plenty of food you can read in 1 Kings. Then it was gone, and the adversaries trod down the sanctuary. We possessed it but a little while.

precepts.text: His angels do his commandments, hearkening unto the voice of his word; the voice of the Most High is his commandments.
precepts.point: Curses means evil: the Lord said, I will bring evil upon this people because they have not hearkened unto my words. Overtake thee means you shall not be able to escape them, and though they cry unto him, he will not hearken.

note.label: Deuteronomy 28: The Blessings and the Curses That Identify Israel

precepts.why:
“But it shall come to pass, if thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God”. Now we do some precepting, word by word. What is the voice of the Lord? “Bless the Lord, ye his angels, that excel in strength, that do his commandments, hearkening unto the voice of his word.” The angels hearken unto his voice by doing his commandments. The voice of the Most High is his commandments.

So to hearken unto his voice means to keep his commandments. Not hearkening to his voice is not keeping them, and that is what brings all these curses upon thee.

precepts.text: Talk no more so exceeding proudly; the Lord is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed.
precepts.point: Curses means evil: the Lord said, I will bring evil upon this people because they have not hearkened unto my words. Overtake thee means you shall not be able to escape them, and though they cry unto him, he will not hearken.

note.label: Deuteronomy 28: The Blessings and the Curses That Identify Israel

precepts.why:
“to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes”: do is the action word. The Most High is a God of doing. “Talk no more so exceeding proudly; let not arrogancy come out of your mouth: for the Lord is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed.” He does not weigh your talk; he weighs your actions.

So do not talk proudly and arrogantly, saying God loves me no matter what, God knows my heart. The Most High had a personal relationship with a few men, Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Samuel and David. Talking like you are one of them is arrogancy coming out of your mouth. What he weighs is whether you observe to do his commandments.

precepts.text: Faith without works is dead; the works are the action of doing the commandments.
precepts.point: Curses means evil: the Lord said, I will bring evil upon this people because they have not hearkened unto my words. Overtake thee means you shall not be able to escape them, and though they cry unto him, he will not hearken.

note.label: Deuteronomy 28: The Blessings and the Curses That Identify Israel

precepts.why:
“But wilt thou know, O vain man, that faith without works is dead?” The works are the action of doing the commandments. Deuteronomy says “observe to do all his commandments and his statutes”, and do is the action word; the Most High is a God of doing.

Faith by itself, saying God knows my heart, is a dead faith. It is the doing of the commandments that gives faith its life, and it is the not doing that brings the curses.

precepts.text: As the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is dead also.
precepts.point: Curses means evil: the Lord said, I will bring evil upon this people because they have not hearkened unto my words. Overtake thee means you shall not be able to escape them, and though they cry unto him, he will not hearken.

note.label: Deuteronomy 28: The Blessings and the Curses That Identify Israel

precepts.why:
“For as the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is dead also.” A body with no spirit in it is a corpse, and faith with no works is the same. The works are the action of doing his commandments, which is exactly what Deuteronomy demands: “observe to do all his commandments and his statutes”.

The Most High is a God of doing, and by him actions are weighed. A faith that does not do the commandments is dead, and a people that does not do them falls under all these curses.

precepts.text: I will bring evil upon this people because they have not hearkened unto my words nor to my law; evil is another way of saying curses.
precepts.point: Curses means evil: the Lord said, I will bring evil upon this people because they have not hearkened unto my words. Overtake thee means you shall not be able to escape them, and though they cry unto him, he will not hearken.

note.label: Deuteronomy 28: The Blessings and the Curses That Identify Israel

precepts.why:
What are curses? “Hear, O earth: behold, I will bring evil upon this people, even the fruit of their thoughts, because they have not hearkened unto my words, nor to my law, but rejected it.” Evil is another way of saying curses. And the reason is the same reason Deuteronomy gives: they have not hearkened unto his words nor to his law; they rejected it.

So “all these curses shall come upon thee” is the Most High bringing evil upon Israel for not hearkening to his voice, which is his commandments, and that evil is the fruit of their own thoughts.

precepts.text: I will bring evil upon them which they shall not be able to escape; the curses shall overtake thee, meaning you will not escape them.
precepts.point: Curses means evil: the Lord said, I will bring evil upon this people because they have not hearkened unto my words. Overtake thee means you shall not be able to escape them, and though they cry unto him, he will not hearken.

note.label: Deuteronomy 28: The Blessings and the Curses That Identify Israel

precepts.why:
“Therefore thus saith the Lord, Behold, I will bring evil upon them, which they shall not be able to escape; and though they shall cry unto me, I will not hearken unto them.” That is what overtake thee means: the curses shall overtake thee, meaning you shall not be able to escape them.

And notice the turn. Israel would not hearken unto his voice, so when the evil comes and they cry unto him, he will not hearken unto them. The curses come upon thee and overtake thee, and there is no escaping them.

precepts.text: Even thus shall the children of Israel eat their defiled bread among the Gentiles, whither I will drive them.
precepts.point: Ezekiel says it plainly: the children of Israel eat their defiled bread among the Gentiles. Others may eat that food, but it is foul for us because we are supposed to eat the best food on the planet, for we are an holy people as Deuteronomy 14 says.

note.label: Deuteronomy 28: The Blessings and the Curses That Identify Israel

precepts.why:
“Cursed shall be the fruit of thy body, and the fruit of thy land, the increase of thy kine, and the flocks of thy sheep.” The fruit of thy body is your children: the same children panicking in front of police, the dozens of children killed by youth gun violence in Chicago in a matter of months. The fruit of thy land, thy kine and thy sheep is the food we eat: it is cursed. Fast food fills our neighborhoods, and where there is no fast food there is a corner store selling unclean meat that causes diseases in us.

Ezekiel says it plainly: “Even thus shall the children of Israel eat their defiled bread among the Gentiles, whither I will drive them.” Defiled bread among the Gentiles, in the lands the Most High drove us to. Others may eat that food, but it is foul for us, because we are supposed to eat the best food on the planet.

precepts.text: Thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God, chosen to be a peculiar people above all the nations upon the earth.
precepts.point: Ezekiel says it plainly: the children of Israel eat their defiled bread among the Gentiles. Others may eat that food, but it is foul for us because we are supposed to eat the best food on the planet, for we are an holy people as Deuteronomy 14 says.

note.label: Deuteronomy 28: The Blessings and the Curses That Identify Israel

precepts.why:
“For thou art an holy people unto the Lord thy God, and the Lord hath chosen thee to be a peculiar people unto himself, above all the nations that are upon the earth.” That is why the cursed food hits us the way it does. Others may eat the fast food and the unclean meat from the corner store, but it is foul for us: an holy people, chosen above all the nations upon the earth, is supposed to eat the best food on the planet.

Instead the fruit of the land, the kine and the sheep are cursed to us, and we eat our defiled bread among the Gentiles, as Ezekiel says. And the fruit of our body, our children, is cursed with it.

precepts.text: Born to a curse and dying with a curse for a portion; and the more we have increased as a people, the worse it has become.
precepts.point: Ecclesiasticus, for you newer people in the Apocrypha, spells it out: we are born under the curses and we die still living under them.

note.label: Deuteronomy 28: The Blessings and the Curses That Identify Israel

precepts.why:
“Cursed shalt thou be when thou comest in, and cursed shalt thou be when thou goest out.” He is talking about Jerusalem, coming in and going out of the city, but it is twofold: it is coming in and going out of life itself.

Ecclesiasticus, for you newer people in the Apocrypha, spells it out: “Woe be unto you, ungodly men, which have forsaken the law of the most high God! for if ye increase, it shall be to your destruction: And if ye be born, ye shall be born to a curse: and if ye die, a curse shall be your portion.” We are born under the curses, coming in, and we die still living under them, going out; a curse is our portion. And the more we have increased as a people, the worse it has become, because “if ye increase, it shall be to your destruction”. All of it for forsaking the law of the most high God.

precepts.text: I have smitten you with blasting and mildew; your gardens, vineyards, fig trees, and olive trees the palmerworm devoured: famine.
precepts.point: Amos shows what the blasting and mildew go into: famine, pestilence after the manner of Egypt, young men slain with the sword, death and destruction.

note.label: Deuteronomy 28: The Blessings and the Curses That Identify Israel

precepts.why:
“The Lord shall smite thee with a consumption, and with a fever, and with an inflammation, and with an extreme burning, and with the sword, and with blasting, and with mildew”. Amos shows what the blasting and the mildew go into: “I have smitten you with blasting and mildew: when your gardens and your vineyards and your fig trees and your olive trees increased, the palmerworm devoured them”. Gardens, vineyards, fig trees and olive trees all devoured: that is famine.

And after all of it, “yet have ye not returned unto me, saith the Lord.” The curses of Deuteronomy 28 are the Most High's own hand, sent to turn Israel back, and they pursue until we return or perish.

precepts.text: I have sent among you the pestilence after the manner of Egypt; your young men have I slain with the sword; yet have ye not returned unto me.
precepts.point: Amos shows what the blasting and mildew go into: famine, pestilence after the manner of Egypt, young men slain with the sword, death and destruction.

note.label: Deuteronomy 28: The Blessings and the Curses That Identify Israel

precepts.why:
“The Lord shall make the pestilence cleave unto thee”: diseases. Amos shows the same hand at work: “I have sent among you the pestilence after the manner of Egypt: your young men have I slain with the sword, and have taken away your horses; and I have made the stink of your camps to come up unto your nostrils”. The pestilence, the sword, young men slain, death and destruction: exactly what Deuteronomy says shall “pursue thee until thou perish.”

“yet have ye not returned unto me, saith the Lord.” The pestilence and the sword are sent by the Most High himself, and they keep pursuing because Israel has not returned to him.

precepts.text: Woe unto them, for they have fled from me; they have not cried unto me with their heart when they howled upon their beds.
precepts.point: Hosea shows the wandering of the blind: we fled from the Most High, we return but not to the Most High, and the end of it is derision in the land of Egypt, which means captivity.

note.label: Deuteronomy 28: The Blessings and the Curses That Identify Israel

precepts.why:
“The Lord shall smite thee with madness, and blindness, and astonishment of heart: And thou shalt grope at noonday, as the blind gropeth in darkness”. Hosea shows the wandering of the blind. “When they shall go, I will spread my net upon them; I will bring them down as the fowls of the heaven; I will chastise them, as their congregation hath heard.” Then: “Woe unto them! for they have fled from me: destruction unto them! because they have transgressed against me: though I have redeemed them, yet they have spoken lies against me.”

We fled from the Most High. He redeemed us, and we spoke lies against him. “And they have not cried unto me with their heart, when they howled upon their beds: they assemble themselves for corn and wine, and they rebel against me.” Even in our howling we do not cry to him with our heart; we gather for corn and wine, for what we can get, and go on rebelling. That is groping at noonday, and it is why “thou shalt not prosper in thy ways”.

precepts.text: They return, but not to the most High; this shall be their derision in the land of Egypt, which means captivity.
precepts.point: Hosea shows the wandering of the blind: we fled from the Most High, we return but not to the Most High, and the end of it is derision in the land of Egypt, which means captivity.

note.label: Deuteronomy 28: The Blessings and the Curses That Identify Israel

precepts.why:
“They return, but not to the most High: they are like a deceitful bow: their princes shall fall by the sword for the rage of their tongue: this shall be their derision in the land of Egypt.” The blind grope and wander. They return, but not to the Most High, like a deceitful bow that does not shoot where it is aimed.

And the end of it is derision in the land of Egypt, which means captivity. That is Deuteronomy 28:29: “thou shalt be only oppressed and spoiled evermore, and no man shall save thee”: going back into bondage.

precepts.text: Ye shall leave your name for a curse unto my chosen; we became a byword and lost our name in the captivity.
precepts.point: Thou shalt become an astonishment, a proverb, and a byword among all nations: Puerto Rican, Dominican, Haitian, Jamaican, African American, gentile. We lost our name and left it for a curse, like it says in Isaiah, while others wear the name and cry anti-Semitic.

note.label: Deuteronomy 28: The Blessings and the Curses That Identify Israel

precepts.why:
“The Lord shall bring thee, and thy king which thou shalt set over thee, unto a nation which neither thou nor thy fathers have known; and there shalt thou serve other gods, wood and stone. And thou shalt become an astonishment, a proverb, and a byword, among all nations whither the Lord shall lead thee.” Puerto Rican, Dominican, Haitian, Jamaican, African American, gentile: those are the bywords. We lost our name in the captivity.

Isaiah says how: “And ye shall leave your name for a curse unto my chosen: for the Lord God shall slay thee, and call his servants by another name”. We left our name for a curse and became a byword among the nations, while others wear the name and cry anti-Semitic. Carried to a nation our fathers never knew, serving other gods of wood and stone, called by every name but our own: that is what becoming a proverb and a byword looks like.

precepts.text: I am the Lord thy God, which brought thee out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage; Egypt means bondage and slavery.
precepts.point: There ye shall be sold unto your enemies for bondmen and bondwomen, and no man shall buy you: buy means redeem. Under the servitude laws a poor brother sold to a stranger could be redeemed by his uncle, his uncle's son, or any of his kin; but in this captivity none of your brothers can redeem you, because they are in bondage right along with you, as verse 29 already said: no man shall save thee.

note.label: Deuteronomy 28: The Blessings and the Curses That Identify Israel

precepts.why:
Here is the nail in the coffin: “And the Lord shall bring thee into Egypt again with ships”. What is Egypt? The scripture defines it right in Deuteronomy 5: “I am the Lord thy God, which brought thee out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage.” Egypt means bondage, slavery.

So the Most High is saying: I will bring you into slavery again, with ships. He brought us out of the house of bondage once; for not hearkening to his voice he brings us into bondage again, and this time by ship.

precepts.text: Woe to the rebellious children that walk to go down into Egypt; Israel could walk to literal Egypt, so the ships carry us to a spiritual Egypt.
precepts.point: There ye shall be sold unto your enemies for bondmen and bondwomen, and no man shall buy you: buy means redeem. Under the servitude laws a poor brother sold to a stranger could be redeemed by his uncle, his uncle's son, or any of his kin; but in this captivity none of your brothers can redeem you, because they are in bondage right along with you, as verse 29 already said: no man shall save thee.

note.label: Deuteronomy 28: The Blessings and the Curses That Identify Israel

precepts.why:
The Egypt of the ships is not the literal land of Egypt, because you can walk to Egypt. Isaiah shows it: “Woe to the rebellious children, saith the Lord, that take counsel, but not of me; and that cover with a covering, but not of my spirit, that they may add sin to sin: That walk to go down into Egypt, and have not asked at my mouth; to strengthen themselves in the strength of Pharaoh, and to trust in the shadow of Egypt!” Israel walked down to Egypt.

If you can walk there, you do not need ships to get there. The false pastors who say we were shipped back across the Red Sea are wrong; the ships of Deuteronomy 28:68 went to a spiritual Egypt, a house of bondage that is not the land by the Nile.

precepts.text: The great city which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt; the spiritual Egypt of the ships is Babylon the great, America.
precepts.point: There ye shall be sold unto your enemies for bondmen and bondwomen, and no man shall buy you: buy means redeem. Under the servitude laws a poor brother sold to a stranger could be redeemed by his uncle, his uncle's son, or any of his kin; but in this captivity none of your brothers can redeem you, because they are in bondage right along with you, as verse 29 already said: no man shall save thee.

note.label: Deuteronomy 28: The Blessings and the Curses That Identify Israel

precepts.why:
Revelation names the spiritual Egypt: “their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city, which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt, where also our Lord was crucified.” There is a great city that is spiritually called Egypt. That is the Egypt the ships carried us into: the greatest country on the face of the earth, America, Babylon the great.

Even their own scholarship confirms who was in Egypt the first time. A treatise on physical geography admits that negroes existed in Egypt in the days of Rameses with the same national features they have now. The Bible says the negroes go into Egypt, bondage, again, and this time it is the spiritual Egypt, reached by ship.

precepts.text: A brother sold to a stranger may be redeemed by his kin; in this captivity no kinsman can redeem you, for all Israel is sold into bondage together.
precepts.point: There ye shall be sold unto your enemies for bondmen and bondwomen, and no man shall buy you: buy means redeem. Under the servitude laws a poor brother sold to a stranger could be redeemed by his uncle, his uncle's son, or any of his kin; but in this captivity none of your brothers can redeem you, because they are in bondage right along with you, as verse 29 already said: no man shall save thee.

note.label: Deuteronomy 28: The Blessings and the Curses That Identify Israel

precepts.why:
“and there ye shall be sold unto your enemies for bondmen and bondwomen, and no man shall buy you.” Buy means redeem. Under the servitude laws, if a brother waxed poor and sold himself unto a stranger, “After that he is sold he may be redeemed again; one of his brethren may redeem him: Either his uncle, or his uncle’s son, may redeem him, or any that is nigh of kin unto him of his family may redeem him; or if he be able, he may redeem himself.”

That is the law of buying back a brother. But in this captivity no man shall buy you: none of your brothers can redeem you, not your uncle, not your uncle's son, not any of your kin, because they are in bondage right along with you. All Israel was sold into bondage together, and there was nobody left free to pay the price.

precepts.text: Thou shalt be only oppressed and spoiled evermore, and no man shall save thee; the quick precept for no man shall buy you.
precepts.point: There ye shall be sold unto your enemies for bondmen and bondwomen, and no man shall buy you: buy means redeem. Under the servitude laws a poor brother sold to a stranger could be redeemed by his uncle, his uncle's son, or any of his kin; but in this captivity none of your brothers can redeem you, because they are in bondage right along with you, as verse 29 already said: no man shall save thee.

note.label: Deuteronomy 28: The Blessings and the Curses That Identify Israel

precepts.why:
“no man shall buy you” has its quick precept earlier in the same chapter: “thou shalt be only oppressed and spoiled evermore, and no man shall save thee.” Buy means redeem, and no man shall save thee says the same thing: sold to your enemies for bondmen and bondwomen, with nobody coming to redeem you.

Under the law a kinsman could redeem a brother sold to a stranger, but here there is no kinsman able, because all Israel went into the bondage together. Oppressed and spoiled evermore, groping at noonday, and no man to save you.

precepts.text: Thou shalt be only oppressed and spoiled evermore, and no man shall save thee; the quick precept for no man shall buy you.
precepts.point: There ye shall be sold unto your enemies for bondmen and bondwomen, and no man shall buy you: buy means redeem. Under the servitude laws a poor brother sold to a stranger could be redeemed by his uncle, his uncle's son, or any of his kin; but in this captivity none of your brothers can redeem you, because they are in bondage right along with you, as verse 29 already said: no man shall save thee.

precepts.why:
“no man shall buy you” has its quick precept earlier in the same chapter: “thou shalt be only oppressed and spoiled evermore, and no man shall save thee.” Buy means redeem, and no man shall save thee says the same thing: sold to your enemies for bondmen and bondwomen, with nobody coming to redeem you.

Under the law a kinsman could redeem a brother sold to a stranger, but here there is no kinsman able, because all Israel went into the bondage together. Oppressed and spoiled evermore, groping at noonday, and no man to save you.

precepts.text: If thou wilt not hearken to observe all his commandments, all these curses shall come upon thee.
precepts.point: You wonder where the Most High was when our babies were used as alligator bait, when we were packed on ships, hung, burnt, and raped in front of our own. His face was hid, because when he would have dwelt among us we went a whoring after other gods, so he left us in the hands of the people that hate us.

note.label: Deuteronomy 31: Moses' Final Charge and the Rebellion Foretold

precepts.why:
The Most High tells Moses his days approach that he must die, and to call Joshua to the tabernacle to receive his charge, and he appears in the pillar of a cloud over the door of the tabernacle. Then he tells Moses straight out: “Behold, thou shalt sleep with thy fathers; and this people will rise up, and go a whoring after the gods of the strangers of the land, whither they go to be among them, and will forsake me, and break my covenant which I have made with them.” The people Moses spent forty years tending will forsake the covenant. Instead of utterly destroying the nations and their gods, they will mingle with the nations and serve their gods.

“Then my anger shall be kindled against them in that day, and I will forsake them, and I will hide my face from them, and they shall be devoured, and many evils and troubles shall befall them”. Those many evils and troubles are the curses we just read through in Deuteronomy 28: “if thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes which I command thee this day; that all these curses shall come upon thee, and overtake thee”. Going a whoring after other gods is not hearkening to his voice, and all these curses are the evils that befall.

You wonder where the Most High was when our babies were used as alligator bait, when we were packed on ships, hung, burnt and raped in front of our own. His face was hid: “I will surely hide my face in that day for all the evils which they shall have wrought, in that they are turned unto other gods.” When he would have dwelt among us, we went a whoring after other gods, so he left us in the hands of the people that hate us. That is why we say in that day, “Are not these evils come upon us, because our God is not among us?”

precepts.text: As the Lord rejoiced over you to do you good, so the Lord will rejoice over you to destroy you, and ye shall be plucked from off the land whither thou goest to possess it.
precepts.point: When ye have transgressed the covenant and served other gods, ye shall perish quickly from off the good land. That is exactly why Israel is not at home right now; we did exactly that. And that is what the waking up is for today: the classes going out all day, the teaching in the streets, trying to bring our people back to the laws of God.

note.label: Joshua 23: Cleave unto the Lord Your God

precepts.why:
Joshua's words are heavy: “as all good things are come upon you, which the Lord your God promised you; so shall the Lord bring upon you all evil things, until he have destroyed you from off this good land”. Moses said it first: “And it shall come to pass, that as the Lord rejoiced over you to do you good, and to multiply you; so the Lord will rejoice over you to destroy you, and to bring you to nought; and ye shall be plucked from off the land whither thou goest to possess it.”

Many come out of Christianity being told God is good all the time, yet the scripture says plainly that the Most High will destroy you when you go off, because that also is what he promised. Not one good thing failed, and the evil things will not fail either.

Plucked from off the land is exactly why Israel is not at home right now; we transgressed the covenant, served other gods, and did exactly that. And that is what the waking up is for today: the classes going out all day, the teaching in the streets, trying to bring our people back to the laws of God.

precepts.text: Cursed shalt thou be when thou comest in, and cursed shalt thou be when thou goest out.
precepts.point: The curse was to be cursed coming in and cursed going out, coming in from war and going out to war, and the same is happening to this very day. Our people do not think we are at war, but when the enemy gives you a false image, a false religion and a false education, slums and ghettos to live in, and bad foods, he is at war with you.

note.label: Judges 2: No League with the Inhabitants of the Land

precepts.why:
“Whithersoever they went out, the hand of the Lord was against them for evil, as the Lord had said, and as the Lord had sworn unto them”. What he had sworn was the curse: “Cursed shalt thou be when thou comest in, and cursed shalt thou be when thou goest out.” Coming in from war and going out to war, cursed both ways, so that they could not any longer stand before their enemies.

The same is happening to this very day. Our people do not think we are at war, but when the enemy gives you a false image, a false religion and a false education, slums and ghettos to live in, and bad foods, he is at war with you. And we are cursed coming in and going out, unable to stand before our enemies, begging them to see us as human.

precepts.text: The Lord shall smite thee with blasting and with mildew; the blasting and the mildew go into famine, exactly what Midian and the children of the east worked on Israel by taking the crops.
precepts.point: When Israel had sown, the Midianites, the Amalekites, and the children of the east came up as grasshoppers for multitude, destroyed the increase of the earth, and left no sustenance for Israel, neither sheep, nor ox, nor ass, and Israel was greatly impoverished. That goes right into the curses.

note.label: Judges 6: The Call of Gideon: Why Is All This Befallen Us

precepts.why:
What Midian did to Israel goes right into the curses. “The Lord shall smite thee with a consumption, and with a fever, and with an inflammation, and with an extreme burning, and with the sword, and with blasting, and with mildew; and they shall pursue thee until thou perish.”

The blasting and the mildew go into famine, and that is exactly what Midian and the children of the east worked on Israel by taking the crops. When Israel had sown, they “came as grasshoppers for multitude”, “destroyed the increase of the earth”, and “left no sustenance for Israel, neither sheep, nor ox, nor ass.” “Israel was greatly impoverished because of the Midianites”: the curse of Deuteronomy 28 carried out by an enemy's hand.

precepts.text: One of the curses for breaking the laws: thy sons and thy daughters shall be given unto another people, and there shall be no might in thine hand.
precepts.point: Moreover the children of Ammon passed over Jordan to fight also against Judah, and against Benjamin, and against the house of Ephraim, which shows those tribes dwelling in their own allotments on the other side; so that Israel was sore distressed.

note.label: Judges 10: Go and Cry unto the Gods Which Ye Have Chosen

precepts.why: “he sold them into the hands of the Philistines, and into the hands of the children of Ammon.” Israel was serving their gods, so the Lord sold Israel to them. This is one of the curses for breaking the laws: “Thy sons and thy daughters shall be given unto another people, and thine eyes shall look, and fail with longing for them all the day long: and there shall be no might in thine hand.” Eighteen years the tribes on the other side Jordan, Reuben, Gad and the half tribe of Manasseh in their allotments in Gilead, were vexed and oppressed: given unto another people, with no might in their hand.

precepts.text: Thou shalt beget sons and daughters, but thou shalt not enjoy them, for they shall go into captivity; the curse of the law was already working on Israel in the land.
precepts.point: Moreover the children of Ammon passed over Jordan to fight also against Judah, and against Benjamin, and against the house of Ephraim, which shows those tribes dwelling in their own allotments on the other side; so that Israel was sore distressed.

note.label: Judges 10: Go and Cry unto the Gods Which Ye Have Chosen

precepts.why: “Thou shalt beget sons and daughters, but thou shalt not enjoy them; for they shall go into captivity.” The curse of the law was already working on Israel while they were still in the land. The Lord sold them into the hands of the Philistines and the children of Ammon; Ammon oppressed Reuben, Gad and the half tribe of Manasseh in Gilead eighteen years, then passed over Jordan against Judah, Benjamin and the house of Ephraim in their own allotments, “so that Israel was sore distressed.” Israel served the gods of those nations, and the Lord gave Israel’s sons and daughters to them.

precepts.text: The stranger gets up very high and Israel comes down very low, the head and the tail; this curse is why we find ourselves in this position, but it does not mean we throw in the towel.
precepts.point: It is important for us to build our legacy and pass it down; that is one of the things we lack in Israel today. Some of us use captivity as an excuse not to better ourselves or build, but that is not what the scriptures say: get the job, further your education, do more for yourself, your family, and the body. Building up your house also means spiritually building it, teaching your wife and children.

note.label: Ruth 1: Naomi and Ruth Return from Moab

precepts.why:
Why do we find ourselves without an inheritance to pass down? “The stranger that is within thee shall get up above thee very high; and thou shalt come down very low. He shall lend to thee, and thou shalt not lend to him: he shall be the head, and thou shalt be the tail.”

The stranger gets up very high and Israel comes down very low; he is the head and we are the tail. This curse is why we are in this position. But it does not mean we throw in the towel: get the job, further your education, do more for yourself, your family and the body.

precepts.text: If thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes, all these curses shall come upon thee and overtake thee.
precepts.point: But if ye will not obey the voice of the Lord, but rebel against the commandment of the Lord, then shall the hand of the Lord be against you, as it was against your fathers. Samuel repeats it because Israelites require repetition.

note.label: 1 Samuel 12: Turn Not Aside From Following the Lord

precepts.why:
Then comes the other side: “But it shall come to pass, if thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes which I command thee this day; that all these curses shall come upon thee, and overtake thee”.

Samuel says it again: “But if ye will not obey the voice of the Lord, but rebel against the commandment of the Lord, then shall the hand of the Lord be against you, as it was against your fathers.” He repeats it because Israelites require repetition. The hand of the Lord against you is these curses coming upon you and overtaking you.

precepts.text: The Lord shall bring thee, and thy king which thou shalt set over thee, unto a nation which neither thou nor thy fathers have known; if you and your king disobey, the Lord sends you and your king into subjection to the other nations.
precepts.point: But if ye will not obey the voice of the Lord, but rebel against the commandment of the Lord, then shall the hand of the Lord be against you, as it was against your fathers. Samuel repeats it because Israelites require repetition.

note.label: 1 Samuel 12: Turn Not Aside From Following the Lord

precepts.why:
Among those curses the king himself is named: “The Lord shall bring thee, and thy king which thou shalt set over thee, unto a nation which neither thou nor thy fathers have known; and there shalt thou serve other gods, wood and stone.”

That is why Samuel puts the people and the king under the same warning. If you and your king disobey, the Lord sends you and your king into subjection to the other nations. The king they demanded so they could be like the nations would go down with them into the hands of the nations.

precepts.text: The LORD shall cause thine enemies to be smitten before thy face and to flee seven ways.
precepts.point: Because David meditated in the law, he knew the Lord was his power source. The Lord had promised that five would chase a hundred and a hundred put ten thousand to flight, that He would cause Israel's enemies to be smitten and to flee seven ways. David leaned wholly on that promise.

note.label: 2 Samuel 5: David Made King Over All Israel

precepts.why:
“The Lord shall cause thine enemies that rise up against thee to be smitten before thy face: they shall come out against thee one way, and flee before thee seven ways.”

The Philistines rose up against David twice in the valley of Rephaim, and twice the Lord caused them to be smitten before him. The second time the Lord himself went out before David, and the host was smitten from Geba to Gazer. David knew this promise from the law, and because he knew it, he knew the Lord was his power source.

precepts.text: All the people of the earth shall see that thou art called by the name of the LORD, and be afraid of thee.
precepts.point: Because David meditated in the law, he knew the Lord was his power source. The Lord had promised that five would chase a hundred and a hundred put ten thousand to flight, that He would cause Israel's enemies to be smitten and to flee seven ways. David leaned wholly on that promise.

note.label: 2 Samuel 5: David Made King Over All Israel

precepts.why:
“And all people of the earth shall see that thou art called by the name of the Lord; and they shall be afraid of thee.”

That was the blessing on Israel when they obeyed, and it was on David. He did “as the Lord had commanded him”, and the Lord went out before him. The nations that came against him saw a people called by the name of the Lord, and they were smitten and afraid.

precepts.text: If Israel will not hearken to do all his commandments, all these curses shall come and overtake them.
precepts.point: The house that was high and mighty would astonish everyone who passed by, and they would ask why the Most High had done this, and the answer is because Israel forsook the Most High who brought their fathers out of Egypt and took hold of other gods. This shows the Most High is not all love, for it says therefore he brought upon them all this evil.

note.label: 1 Kings 9: The Most High Appears to Solomon a Second Time

precepts.why:
“But it shall come to pass, if thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes which I command thee this day; that all these curses shall come upon thee, and overtake thee”.

This is the same warning Moses gave in the law, and the Most High gives it again to Solomon: “if ye shall at all turn from following me, ye or your children, and will not keep my commandments and my statutes”, “Then will I cut off Israel out of the land which I have given them”. Disobedience brings the curse of scattering, and it reaches not only that generation but the seed after them.

The Most High is not all love. When they ask why this came, the answer is, “Because they forsook the Lord their God”, “therefore hath the Lord brought upon them all this evil.”

precepts.text: Israel shall become an astonishment, a proverb, and a byword among all nations where the Most High shall lead them.
precepts.point: The house that was high and mighty would astonish everyone who passed by, and they would ask why the Most High had done this, and the answer is because Israel forsook the Most High who brought their fathers out of Egypt and took hold of other gods. This shows the Most High is not all love, for it says therefore he brought upon them all this evil.

note.label: 1 Kings 9: The Most High Appears to Solomon a Second Time

precepts.why:
“And thou shalt become an astonishment, a proverb, and a byword, among all nations whither the Lord shall lead thee.”

The Most High told Solomon the same: “Israel shall be a proverb and a byword among all people: And at this house, which is high, every one that passeth by it shall be astonished, and shall hiss”. The house that was high and mighty would astonish everyone who passed by.

They would ask, “Why hath the Lord done thus unto this land, and to this house?” and the answer: Israel forsook the Most High who brought their fathers out of the land of Egypt, and took hold of other gods. The curse of the law and the word to Solomon are one.

precepts.text: A curse of disobedience is that the carcass becomes meat for the fowls of the air and the beasts of the earth, with none to fray them away.
precepts.point: Any of Ahab's house dying in the city the dogs would eat, and any dying in the field the fowls of the air would eat, matching the curses spoken in the law.

note.label: 1 Kings 21: Naboth's Vineyard and the Judgment on Ahab

precepts.why:
“And thy carcase shall be meat unto all fowls of the air, and unto the beasts of the earth, and no man shall fray them away.” That is one of the curses of disobedience in the law.

The Most High declared, “The dogs shall eat Jezebel by the wall of Jezreel. Him that dieth of Ahab in the city the dogs shall eat; and him that dieth in the field shall the fowls of the air eat.” The judgment on Ahab’s house matches the curse spoken in the law: their carcases left as meat for the beasts and the birds.

precepts.text: If Israel hearkens diligently to the voice of the Lord to do his commandments, the Most High will set them on high above all nations of the earth, as happened under David.
precepts.point: Moab rebels against Israel after the death of Ahab. Nations that had been subdued under David and brought under tribute begin to break away, because Israel no longer walks in the blessing that came from serving the Most High.

note.label: 2 Kings 1: Ahaziah Inquires of Beelzebub and Dies

precepts.why:
The law says, “if thou shalt hearken diligently unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe and to do all his commandments”, then “the Lord thy God will set thee on high above all nations of the earth.”

That is what happened under David, when Moab and the other nations were brought under Israel. Being set on high above the nations depends on hearkening to the voice of the Lord. After Ahab, Israel was not hearkening, and so Moab no longer stayed beneath them.

precepts.text: The Lord causes the enemies that rise up against Israel to be smitten before their face when the nation keeps his commandments.
precepts.point: Moab rebels against Israel after the death of Ahab. Nations that had been subdued under David and brought under tribute begin to break away, because Israel no longer walks in the blessing that came from serving the Most High.

note.label: 2 Kings 1: Ahaziah Inquires of Beelzebub and Dies

precepts.why:
“The Lord shall cause thine enemies that rise up against thee to be smitten before thy face: they shall come out against thee one way, and flee before thee seven ways.”

When Israel keeps his commandments, the enemies that rise up are smitten before them, as Moab was smitten under David. Moab rising up and rebelling after the death of Ahab shows that the nation was no longer under that blessing.

precepts.text: But if Israel will not hearken to the voice of the Lord to do his commandments, all these curses shall come upon them and overtake them.
precepts.point: Moab rebels against Israel after the death of Ahab. Nations that had been subdued under David and brought under tribute begin to break away, because Israel no longer walks in the blessing that came from serving the Most High.

note.label: 2 Kings 1: Ahaziah Inquires of Beelzebub and Dies

precepts.why:
“But it shall come to pass, if thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes which I command thee this day; that all these curses shall come upon thee, and overtake thee.”

The same chapter that promised to set Israel on high above all nations promised the curses if they would not hearken. Under Ahab they did not, and the curses began to overtake them. Moab breaking away is part of that.

precepts.text: The Lord causes a disobedient Israel to be smitten before their enemies and scattered, their carcasses meat for the fowls of the air, which is the same judgment pronounced on the house of Ahab.
precepts.point: Moab rebels against Israel after the death of Ahab. Nations that had been subdued under David and brought under tribute begin to break away, because Israel no longer walks in the blessing that came from serving the Most High.

note.label: 2 Kings 1: Ahaziah Inquires of Beelzebub and Dies

precepts.why:
“The Lord shall cause thee to be smitten before thine enemies: thou shalt go out one way against them, and flee seven ways before them: and shalt be removed into all the kingdoms of the earth. And thy carcase shall be meat unto all fowls of the air, and unto the beasts of the earth, and no man shall fray them away.”

This is the blessing of verse 7 turned around. Instead of the enemy fleeing seven ways before Israel, a disobedient Israel flees seven ways before the enemy and is scattered. And the carcase given as meat for the fowls of the air is the same judgment pronounced on the house of Ahab. After Ahab’s death Moab rebels, and the curse is on its way.

precepts.text: The Lord causes the enemies that rise up against Israel to be smitten before their face when the nation keeps his commandments.
precepts.point: This victory is a testament to how great a people Israel was when the hand of the Lord was with them. When Israel was in its right mind and its prayers went forth, the Lord fought for them, which is part of why the heathen nations, and Moab in particular, have hated Israel to this day.

note.label: 2 Kings 3: Three Kings and the Water in the Ditches

precepts.why:
“The Lord shall cause thine enemies that rise up against thee to be smitten before thy face: they shall come out against thee one way, and flee before thee seven ways.” That is the promise to Israel when the nation keeps his commandments, and here it is in the field against Moab.

The Moabites came out one way. Rising early, they saw the sun on the water “as red as blood” and said, “This is blood: the kings are surely slain, and they have smitten one another: now therefore, Moab, to the spoil.” They ran toward the camp expecting to gather the plunder of dead men. Instead “the Israelites rose up and smote the Moabites, so that they fled before them”, and Israel went forward smiting them even into their own country, beating down the cities, stopping the wells and felling the good trees.

This is a testament to how great a people Israel was when the hand of the Lord was with them. When Israel was in its right mind and its prayers went forth, the Lord fought for them and their enemies were smitten before their face. That is part of why the heathen nations, and Moab in particular, have hated Israel to this day.

precepts.text: In the siege and straitness of the enemy, a disobedient Israel shall eat the fruit of their own body, the flesh of their sons and daughters, which is the curse fulfilled in this famine.
precepts.point: The woman tells how another woman said, give thy son that we may eat him today, and we will eat my son tomorrow, so they boiled and ate her son, but the next day the other woman hid her son. When the king hears this, he rends his clothes, and the people see he has sackcloth upon his flesh, and he swears that the head of Elisha shall not stand on him this day.

note.label: 2 Kings 6: The Floating Axe Head and the Blinded Host

precepts.why:
“And thou shalt eat the fruit of thine own body, the flesh of thy sons and of thy daughters, which the Lord thy God hath given thee, in the siege, and in the straitness, wherewith thine enemies shall distress thee:” That is the curse on a disobedient Israel, and in Samaria it came to pass.

Ben-hadad king of Syria besieged Samaria, and the famine was so great that “an ass’s head was sold for fourscore pieces of silver, and the fourth part of a cab of dove’s dung for five pieces of silver.” A woman cried to the king on the wall and told him, “This woman said unto me, Give thy son, that we may eat him to day, and we will eat my son to morrow. So we boiled my son, and did eat him”. The next day the other woman hid her son.

The siege, the straitness, the enemy distressing them, and mothers eating the flesh of their sons: the curse fulfilled. The king had no help to give, “If the Lord do not help thee, whence shall I help thee?” He rent his clothes, the people saw “he had sackcloth within upon his flesh”, and he swore that the head of Elisha would not stand on him that day.

precepts.text: No man can buy or redeem the nation out of its condition, for the curses come from forsaking the Most High.
precepts.point: These settler nations feared the Most High yet served their graven images to this day, and as a nation Israel does the same, serving the gods of the nations.

note.label: 2 Kings 17: The Carrying Away of Israel

precepts.why:
The law says, “if thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes which I command thee this day; that all these curses shall come upon thee, and overtake thee.”

The curses come from forsaking the Most High, so no man can buy or redeem the nation out of its condition. No nation and no treaty can do it. The covenant said, “the Lord your God ye shall fear; and he shall deliver you out of the hand of all your enemies.” Only turning to the Most High can.

“Howbeit they did not hearken, but they did after their former manner.” The settler nations feared the Lord and served their graven images to this day, and as a nation Israel does the same, serving the gods of the nations. So the curses stay on them.

precepts.text: The captivity comes because Israel would not hearken to the voice of the Most High.
precepts.point: The reason given again is that they obeyed not the voice of the Most High but transgressed His covenant and all Moses commanded.

note.label: 2 Kings 18: Hezekiah and the Assyrian Threat

precepts.why:
The law says, “if thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes which I command thee this day; that all these curses shall come upon thee, and overtake thee.”

Samaria was besieged in Hezekiah’s fourth year and taken at the end of three years, and the king of Assyria carried Israel away into Halah, Habor by the river of Gozan, and the cities of the Medes. Israel was carried away in stages, not all at once.

The reason is given again, in the words of the curse: “Because they obeyed not the voice of the Lord their God, but transgressed his covenant, and all that Moses the servant of the Lord commanded, and would not hear them, nor do them.” The captivity comes because Israel would not hearken.

precepts.text: If they will not hearken to do all the commandments, all these curses shall come upon them, the wrath Josiah heard when the book was read.
precepts.point: Josiah commands Hilkiah and his servants to inquire of the Most High for him and the people, for great is the wrath kindled against them because their fathers did not hearken to this book.

note.label: 2 Kings 22: Josiah and the Book of the Law

precepts.why:
The law says, “if thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes which I command thee this day; that all these curses shall come upon thee, and overtake thee.”

This is the wrath Josiah heard when the book was read. Manasseh and Amon were so wicked that the very book of the law had been lost, until Hilkiah found it in the house of the Lord. The king was meant to read the law before all the people, and the wicked kings had not done it.

When Shaphan read it before him, Josiah rent his clothes and sent to inquire of the Lord, “for great is the wrath of the Lord that is kindled against us, because our fathers have not hearkened unto the words of this book, to do according unto all that which is written concerning us.” The curses were written concerning them, and they had come.

precepts.text: When the Most High is against a people, their ox is slain before their eyes and their ass is violently taken away.
precepts.point: They took away much cattle and a hundred thousand captives, for the war was of the Most High; this is the curse of Deuteronomy 28 falling on the enemy instead of on us.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 5: The Tribes East of Jordan and Their Captivity

precepts.why:
“Thine ox shall be slain before thine eyes, and thou shalt not eat thereof: thine ass shall be violently taken away from before thy face, and shall not be restored to thee: thy sheep shall be given unto thine enemies, and thou shalt have none to rescue them.” When the Most High is against a people, this is what happens to them.

Here the curse of Deuteronomy 28 falls on the enemy instead of on us. Reuben, Gad and the half tribe of Manasseh made war with the Hagarites, “And they were helped against them”, “for they cried to God in the battle, and he was intreated of them; because they put their trust in him.” “And they took away their cattle; of their camels fifty thousand, and of sheep two hundred and fifty thousand, and of asses two thousand, and of men an hundred thousand.” “For there fell down many slain, because the war was of God.”

precepts.text: A curse on the seed is the enemy besieging the gates until the high and fenced walls come down wherein they trusted.
precepts.point: Asa has an army of 300,000 of Judah and 280,000 of Benjamin, all mighty men of valor.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 14: Asa Seeks the Most High and Finds Rest

precepts.why:
“And he shall besiege thee in all thy gates, until thy high and fenced walls come down, wherein thou trustedst, throughout all thy land.”

That is a curse on the seed: the enemy besieging the gates until the high and fenced walls come down.
