Asa's day was the other side of it. “because we have sought the Lord our God, we have sought him, and he hath given us rest on every side.” So the walls went up, “So they built and prospered”, and Asa had an army of 300,000 out of Judah and 280,000 out of Benjamin, “all these were mighty men of valour.”

precepts.text: Every sickness not written in the book of the law the Most High would bring upon a disobedient people until they be destroyed.
precepts.point: His own body would be struck: he would have great sickness by disease of his bowels, until his bowels fell out by reason of the sickness day by day. This is what it looks like to mess with the Most High.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 21: Jehoram's Wicked Reign

precepts.why:
“Also every sickness, and every plague, which is not written in the book of this law, them will the Lord bring upon thee, until thou be destroyed.”

That is what came on Jehoram. Elijah's writing charged him with walking “in the way of the kings of Israel”, making Judah and Jerusalem “to go a whoring, like to the whoredoms of the house of Ahab”, and slaying his brethren “which were better than thyself.” So: “with a great plague will the Lord smite thy people, and thy children, and thy wives, and all thy goods.”

And his own body was struck: “thou shalt have great sickness by disease of thy bowels, until thy bowels fall out by reason of the sickness day by day.” This is what it looks like to mess with the Most High.

precepts.text: The curse said the Most High would bring the king they set over themselves into a nation they had not known, to serve other gods of wood and stone.
precepts.point: They take Manasseh among the thorns, bind him with chains, and carry him to Babylon. The kings of Israel that were once kings are brought down into captivity, exactly as the curses warned.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 33: Manasseh's Wickedness and His Humbling

precepts.why:
The curse said: “The Lord shall bring thee, and thy king which thou shalt set over thee, unto a nation which neither thou nor thy fathers have known; and there shalt thou serve other gods, wood and stone.”

That came upon Manasseh. “And the Lord spake to Manasseh, and to his people: but they would not hearken.” So the Lord “brought upon them the captains of the host of the king of Assyria, which took Manasseh among the thorns, and bound him with fetters, and carried him to Babylon.” The kings of Israel that were once kings were brought down into captivity, exactly as the curses warned.

precepts.text: The Lord would bring a nation from far, swift as the eagle, of fierce countenance, which would not regard the person of the old nor show favour to the young.
precepts.point: They burn the house of God, break down the walls of Jerusalem, burn its palaces, and destroy all the goodly vessels, exactly the fierce nation the curses warned of.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 36: The Captivity of Judah into Babylon

precepts.why:
The curses of the law said it before it happened: “The Lord shall bring a nation against thee from far, from the end of the earth, as swift as the eagle flieth; a nation whose tongue thou shalt not understand; A nation of fierce countenance, which shall not regard the person of the old, nor shew favour to the young.”

That nation is the king of the Chaldees. He slew their young men with the sword in the house of their sanctuary, and “had no compassion upon young man or maiden, old man, or him that stooped for age.” No regard for the old, no favour to the young, exactly as written.

The Most High gave them all into Nebuchadnezzar’s hand. The vessels of the house of God, the treasures of the house of the Lord and of the king and his princes, were brought to Babylon; the house of God was burnt and the wall of Jerusalem broken down. This is the fierce nation the curses warned of, come upon Judah.

precepts.text: The Most High foretold Israel would be scattered among all people from one end of the earth unto the other.
precepts.point: This is the span of the Persian empire, and Israel was scattered all through it, from India to Ethiopia, not concentrated in one place but spread out during the captivity, which shows we have history in these lands.

note.label: Esther 8: The Decree Reversed for the Jews

precepts.why:
The decree went to “the provinces which are from India unto Ethiopia, an hundred twenty and seven provinces, unto every province according to the writing thereof, and unto every people after their language, and to the Jews according to their writing, and according to their language.” That is the span of the Persian empire, and the Jews had to be written to in all of it. Israel was scattered all through it, from India to Ethiopia, not concentrated in one place but spread out during the captivity.

The Most High had foretold it: “the Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other”. A hundred twenty and seven provinces with Jews in them is that scattering. It also shows we have history in these lands: from India to Ethiopia, Israel was there.

precepts.text: The Most High foretold a nation of fierce countenance that would not regard the person of the old nor shew favour to the young.
precepts.point: This sounds exactly like the curses laid out for our people in Deuteronomy 28, where the enemy shows no favor toward the young or the old. Both the ancient and the present generation were marked for the grave in one day.

note.label: Esther 13: The Decree of Destruction and the Prayer of Mardocheus

precepts.why:
The decree marks all the Jews, “with their wives and children”, for the sword “without all mercy and pity”, so that “they, who of old and now also are malicious, may in one day with violence go into the grave”. The ancient and the present generation together, marked for the grave in one day.

That sounds exactly like the curses laid out for our people. “The Lord shall bring a nation against thee from far, from the end of the earth, as swift as the eagle flieth; a nation whose tongue thou shalt not understand; A nation of fierce countenance, which shall not regard the person of the old, nor shew favour to the young”. The Most High foretold an enemy that would show no favor toward the young or the old, and Haman's decree is that enemy: no mercy, no pity, wives and children with the men.

The letter is not only Persian history; it is the curse of Deuteronomy 28 falling on our people.

precepts.text: The Most High warned Israel would be carried to a nation they knew not, and there serve other gods, wood and stone.
precepts.point: The heathen open their mouths to set forth the praises of idols and to magnify a fleshly king for ever. The Persians, Assyrians, and Egyptians all magnified themselves when they were in power.

note.label: Esther 14: The Prayer of Esther

precepts.why:
Esther confesses the true reason for the captivity: “we have sinned before thee: therefore hast thou given us into the hands of our enemies, Because we worshipped their gods: O Lord, thou art righteous.” She does not blame the Persians; she says the Most High is righteous in what he did.

That is exactly what he warned. “The Lord shall bring thee, and thy king which thou shalt set over thee, unto a nation which neither thou nor thy fathers have known; and there shalt thou serve other gods, wood and stone.” Israel would be carried to a nation they knew not, and there they would serve other gods. Esther in Persia is that warning come to pass, and her confession is the curse owned.

This is the same confession our people must make about why we went into captivity and are under these curses: we sinned, we worshipped their gods, and the Lord is righteous.

precepts.text: The Lord would scatter Israel among all people, and there they would serve other gods, which neither they nor their fathers had known.
precepts.point: The heathen open their mouths to set forth the praises of idols and to magnify a fleshly king for ever. The Persians, Assyrians, and Egyptians all magnified themselves when they were in power.

note.label: Esther 14: The Prayer of Esther

precepts.why:
“And the Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other; and there thou shalt serve other gods, which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone.” Esther's words, “we worshipped their gods”, are the fulfilling of this. The scattering and the serving of other gods came together, as the Most High said they would, and so she says, “thou art righteous.”

Yet the enemy is not satisfied with that. “Nevertheless it satisfieth them not, that we are in bitter captivity: but they have stricken hands with their idols, That they will abolish the thing that thou with thy mouth hast ordained, and destroy thine inheritance, and stop the mouth of them that praise thee”. It is the same thing today: they are not satisfied with us serving in captivity, they want to destroy our people.

And they “open the mouths of the heathen to set forth the praises of the idols, and to magnify a fleshly king for ever.” The Persians, the Assyrians and the Egyptians all magnified themselves when they were in power. The scattered nation serving wood and stone is the nation the heathen magnify themselves over.

precepts.text: Life hangs in doubt, fearing day and night, wishing morning were evening and evening were morning.
precepts.point: His flesh is clothed with worms and clods of dust; his skin is broken and become loathsome. Satan smote him in his skin, and his flesh was covered in boils, pus, and worms.

note.label: Job 7: Job's Anguish and the Shortness of His Days

precepts.why:
Job says, “When I lie down, I say, When shall I arise, and the night be gone? and I am full of tossings to and fro unto the dawning of the day.” His spirit is in such anguish he cannot rest. That is the tossing of Deuteronomy 28: “And thy life shall hang in doubt before thee; and thou shalt fear day and night, and shalt have none assurance of thy life”.

Life hangs in doubt, fearing day and night, wishing morning were evening and evening were morning. When it is day Job wishes it were night, and when it is night he wishes it were day. Satan smote him in his skin, and his flesh was covered in boils, pus, and worms, “clothed with worms and clods of dust”, with months of vanity and wearisome nights appointed to him.

precepts.text: Thou shalt grope at noonday as the blind gropeth in darkness, and thou shalt not prosper in thy ways, describing how our people stagger though the light is brightest.
precepts.point: Look at what they did to the northern kingdom, taking away the heart of the chief, the mighty warriors, infiltrating them with alcohol and diseases, then sending them on their way with smallpox blankets so they stagger like drunken men; many of our northern kingdom brothers, especially Gad, deal with drunkenness, opium, and the war on drugs, but we keep the commandments and are coming back to be straightened out.

note.label: Job 12: With God Is Strength and Wisdom

precepts.why:
“And thou shalt grope at noonday, as the blind gropeth in darkness, and thou shalt not prosper in thy ways: and thou shalt be only oppressed and spoiled evermore, and no man shall save thee.” Our people stagger though the light is brightest. That is “They grope in the dark without light, and he maketh them to stagger like a drunken man”; this is Deuteronomy 28.

He increaseth the nations and destroyeth them; he enlargeth the nations and straiteneth them again. This is us, Israel, for the curses destroyed us to the point where we do not realize we are the Israelites, God's chosen people, and then he heals us back up again. You see the aged of the people lose their wisdom and the strong lose their might, like Muhammad Ali and others we thought were noblemen for the nation of Israel.

Look at what they did to the northern kingdom: taking away the heart of the chief, the mighty warriors, infiltrating them with alcohol and diseases, then sending them on their way with smallpox blankets so they stagger like drunken men. Many of our northern kingdom brothers, especially Gad, deal with drunkenness, opium, and the war on drugs. Oppressed and spoiled, and no man shall save us; but we keep the commandments and are coming back to be straightened out.

precepts.text: When Israel is wicked, curses fall as a nation: the ox slain before your eyes, the ass taken away, the seed given to the enemy with none to rescue.
precepts.point: Their bulls gender and fail not, their cow calveth and casteth not her calf. They are even prosperous in their animals.

note.label: Job 21: Why the Wicked Prosper

precepts.why:
“Thine ox shall be slain before thine eyes, and thou shalt not eat thereof: thine ass shall be violently taken away from before thy face, and shall not be restored to thee: thy sheep shall be given unto thine enemies, and thou shalt have none to rescue them.” When Israel is wicked, curses fall as a nation: the ox slain before your eyes, the ass taken away, the seed given to the enemy with none to rescue.

That is the opposite of what Job sees in the wicked: “Their bull gendereth, and faileth not; their cow calveth, and casteth not her calf.” They are even prosperous in their animals, while the rod of God is not upon them. This is going twofold, dealing with the wicked of Israel and the wicked of Esau, and this passage is the pride of Esau; Israel's wickedness brings the curse on its cattle, while Esau's beasts fail not.

precepts.text: A nation swift as the eagle, of fierce countenance, whose symbol is the eagle, shall eat the fruit of your cattle and land until you are destroyed.
precepts.point: They drive away the ass of the fatherless and take the widow's ox for a pledge. They turn the needy out of the way, and the poor of the earth hide themselves together.

note.label: Job 24: The Crimes of the Oppressor

precepts.why:
The oppressor Job describes was foretold in the curses: “The Lord shall bring a nation against thee from far, from the end of the earth, as swift as the eagle flieth; a nation whose tongue thou shalt not understand; A nation of fierce countenance, which shall not regard the person of the old, nor shew favour to the young”. A nation swift as the eagle, whose symbol is the eagle.

“And he shall eat the fruit of thy cattle, and the fruit of thy land, until thou be destroyed: which also shall not leave thee either corn, wine, or oil, or the increase of thy kine, or flocks of thy sheep, until he have destroyed thee.” That is the one who violently takes away flocks and feeds thereof, takes the widow's ox for a pledge and turns the needy out of the way: eating the fruit of our cattle and our land until we are destroyed.

precepts.text: Thy sons and daughters given to another people, and thine eyes shall look and fail with longing for them all day long.
precepts.point: They which make oil within their walls and tread their winepresses still suffer thirst. This is the curse where you plant vineyards and do not eat from them, left neither corn nor wine.

note.label: Job 24: The Crimes of the Oppressor

precepts.why:
“They pluck the fatherless from the breast, and take a pledge of the poor.” That is a curse on us: “Thy sons and thy daughters shall be given unto another people, and thine eyes shall look, and fail with longing for them all the day long: and there shall be no might in thine hand.”

The fatherless plucked from the breast are our sons and daughters given to another people, while our eyes look and fail with longing for them all the day long and there is no might in our hand to stop it. The oppressor's crime is the curse we were told would come.

precepts.text: In the morning you shall say, would God it were even, and at evening, would God it were morning; you cannot tell if day or night is worse.
precepts.point: They are of those that rebel against the light; they know not the ways thereof nor abide in the paths thereof. The murderer rising with the light killeth the poor and needy, and in the night is as a thief. He will kill you in broad daylight.

note.label: Job 24: The Crimes of the Oppressor

precepts.why:
“The murderer rising with the light killeth the poor and needy, and in the night is as a thief.” Day or night there is no safety, which is the curse: “In the morning thou shalt say, Would God it were even! and at even thou shalt say, Would God it were morning! for the fear of thine heart wherewith thou shalt fear, and for the sight of thine eyes which thou shalt see.”

You cannot tell if day or night is worse. The murderer kills in broad daylight and comes as a thief by night, so the fear of the heart and the sight of the eyes never let up.

precepts.text: Thy life shall hang in doubt before thee, and thou shalt fear day and night, and have none assurance of thy life.
precepts.point: And if it be not so now, who will make Job a liar and make his speech nothing worth? The prophecy will come true because Job is speaking as the mouthpiece of God.

note.label: Job 24: The Crimes of the Oppressor

precepts.why:
Job says “he riseth up, and no man is sure of life.” That is the curse: “And thy life shall hang in doubt before thee; and thou shalt fear day and night, and shalt have none assurance of thy life”.

No assurance of life, failing eyes and sorrow of mind. The mighty one draws with his power and rises up, and under him our life hangs in doubt and we fear day and night. Job is describing the curse we live under.

precepts.text: Among the nations we find no ease but a trembling heart, failing eyes, sorrow of mind, and life hanging in doubt with fear day and night; this includes depression that many of our people suffer, and the constant fear even a law-abiding person feels when police pull up behind them.
precepts.point: The sorrows of death describe the curses of the scattering.

note.label: Psalm 18: The Song of the Elect in the Last Days

precepts.why:
“The sorrows of death compassed me, and the floods of ungodly men made me afraid.” The sorrows of death describe the curses of the scattering, and Moses laid them out: “And among these nations shalt thou find no ease, neither shall the sole of thy foot have rest: but the Lord shall give thee there a trembling heart, and failing of eyes, and sorrow of mind”.

“And thy life shall hang in doubt before thee; and thou shalt fear day and night, and shalt have none assurance of thy life”. Among the nations we find no ease, but a trembling heart, failing eyes, sorrow of mind, and life hanging in doubt with fear day and night.

That includes the depression so many of our people suffer, and the constant fear even a law-abiding person feels when the police pull up behind them. Those are the sorrows of death and the sorrows of hell compassing us about, and it is in that distress that David called upon the Lord, and he heard his voice out of his temple.

precepts.text: Because thou servedst not the Lord thy God with joyfulness and gladness of heart, therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies, which is who our people serve now, even on Sundays when they think they are serving the Most High but are serving the man that put us into captivity and stole the identity of the black Messiah.
precepts.point: It is the righteous that must rejoice in the Lord, us that understand who the Most High is, that He is a black man according to the Bible, that His son is black, and that the Israelites are black. This is how we rejoice in the Lord, not to Cesare Borgia. Praise the Lord with harp, sing unto Him with the psaltery and an instrument of ten strings, sing unto Him a new song, play skillfully with a loud noise.

note.label: Psalm 33: Rejoice in the Lord O Ye Righteous

precepts.why:
“Rejoice in the Lord, O ye righteous: for praise is comely for the upright.” Comely means beautiful. We must remember to rejoice, because that is why we came into captivity in the first place: “Because thou servedst not the Lord thy God with joyfulness, and with gladness of heart, for the abundance of all things”. Therefore we were made to serve our enemies, which is who our people serve now, even on Sundays when they think they are serving the Most High. They are serving the man that put us into captivity and stole the identity of the black Messiah.

Our people do have a spirit to rejoice in the Lord, but they are not rejoicing to him in church on Sunday; they are rejoicing to Cesare Borgia. The spirit within them to serve is a godly spirit, because we are of God, but they are not serving him in spirit and in truth, because they have no idea who the Most High is.

It is the righteous that must rejoice in the Lord: us that understand who the Most High is, that he is a black man according to the Bible, that his son is black, and that the Israelites are black. That is how we rejoice in the Lord, with the harp, the psaltery and the instrument of ten strings, a new song played skilfully with a loud noise, and not to Cesare Borgia.

precepts.text: Hearken diligently to His commandments and He sets thee on high and causes thine enemies to be smitten before thy face, fleeing seven ways.
precepts.point: Treading down the enemy through His name is not screaming a name you believe is the name of the Lord. The name means keeping the commandments.

note.label: Psalm 44: We Got Not the Land by Our Own Sword

precepts.why:
“Thou art my King, O God: command deliverances for Jacob. Through thee will we push down our enemies: through thy name will we tread them under that rise up against us.” Moses shows how the Most High commands that deliverance: “if thou shalt hearken diligently unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe and to do all his commandments which I command thee this day, that the Lord thy God will set thee on high above all nations of the earth”. Then: “The Lord shall cause thine enemies that rise up against thee to be smitten before thy face: they shall come out against thee one way, and flee before thee seven ways.”

Treading down the enemy through his name is not screaming a name you believe is the name of the Lord. The name means keeping the commandments: hearken diligently and observe to do them, and he sets thee on high and smites the enemies that rise up against thee, so they flee seven ways.

We cannot go it alone. Those who take up arms on their own without the Most High have their examples of failure; men who went to make a name for themselves fell. It is through him that we push down our enemies.

precepts.text: If thou wilt not hearken, the curses come; thou shalt flee seven ways and be removed into all kingdoms of the earth.
precepts.point: He sold His people for nothing and did not increase His wealth by their price.

note.label: Psalm 44: We Got Not the Land by Our Own Sword

precepts.why:
“But thou hast cast off, and put us to shame; and goest not forth with our armies. Thou makest us to turn back from the enemy”. This is the curse Moses wrote: “if thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes which I command thee this day; that all these curses shall come upon thee, and overtake thee”. Among them: “The Lord shall cause thee to be smitten before thine enemies: thou shalt go out one way against them, and flee seven ways before them: and shalt be removed into all the kingdoms of the earth.”

Turned back from the enemy, given like sheep appointed for meat, scattered among the heathen: that is being smitten before thine enemies, fleeing seven ways and being removed into all the kingdoms of the earth. He sold his people for nought because we would not hearken. The enemy's power to spoil us is the curse for our sins.

precepts.text: Thou shalt become an astonishment, a proverb, and a byword among all nations whither the Most High leads thee.
precepts.point: The shaking of the head is because we are an astonishment to our enemies. We went into slavery, our names were changed, our culture and lands were taken, and another nation took our name.

note.label: Psalm 44: We Got Not the Land by Our Own Sword

precepts.why:
“Thou makest us a byword among the heathen, a shaking of the head among the people.” That is the curse: “thou shalt become an astonishment, a proverb, and a byword, among all nations whither the Lord shall lead thee.”

The shaking of the head is because we are an astonishment to our enemies. We went into slavery, our names were changed, our culture and lands were taken, and another nation took our name. Israel became a reproach, a scorn, a derision, a byword, and a shaking of the head among the heathen the Most High led us to.

precepts.text: Among these nations thou shalt find no ease; the Most High gives a trembling heart, failing eyes, sorrow of mind, and thy life hangs in doubt.
precepts.point: The fearfulness and trembling and horror are written in the curses, the curses we did not learn in the Christian church. Many of the scriptures come back to these curses.

note.label: Psalm 55: Cast Thy Burden Upon the Lord

precepts.why:
“My heart is sore pained within me: and the terrors of death are fallen upon me. Fearfulness and trembling are come upon me, and horror hath overwhelmed me.” That fearfulness, trembling and horror are written in the curses: “among these nations shalt thou find no ease, neither shall the sole of thy foot have rest: but the Lord shall give thee there a trembling heart, and failing of eyes, and sorrow of mind: And thy life shall hang in doubt before thee; and thou shalt fear day and night, and shalt have none assurance of thy life”.

These are the curses we did not learn in the Christian church, and many of the scriptures come back to them. Think about the condition we are in today: even keeping the commandments, we still suffer the same oppression, though the Most High covers those that keep them. When you drive, police will still jump behind you and run your plates, so make sure your tags are legal and not expired. A trembling heart and a life hanging in doubt is where David's heart is in Psalm 55.

precepts.text: Hearken diligently to His commandments and the Most High sets thee on high above all nations; blessed in the city and field, and the fruit of thy body and thy ground and thy cattle.
precepts.point: This is what the psalmist was referring to: when we keep the commandments of God, we as a nation come under the blessings of Deuteronomy 28. The ground yielding its increase is exactly that promise.

note.label: Psalm 67: The Nation Blessed in Rulership

precepts.why:
“Then shall the earth yield her increase; and God, even our own God, shall bless us.” This is what the psalmist was referring to: when we keep the commandments of God, we as a nation come under the blessings of Deuteronomy 28. “And it shall come to pass, if thou shalt hearken diligently unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe and to do all his commandments which I command thee this day, that the Lord thy God will set thee on high above all nations of the earth: And all these blessings shall come on thee, and overtake thee”.

“Blessed shalt thou be in the city, and blessed shalt thou be in the field. Blessed shall be the fruit of thy body, and the fruit of thy ground, and the fruit of thy cattle, the increase of thy kine, and the flocks of thy sheep. Blessed shall be thy basket and thy store.” The ground yielding its increase is exactly that promise, the fruit of thy ground. Our own God blesses us when we hearken diligently, and all the ends of the earth shall fear him.

precepts.text: Hearken diligently and the blessings overtake thee as a nation; the Most High causes thine enemies to be smitten before thy face, coming out one way and fleeing seven ways.
precepts.point: This is going into the blessing again. Today people say they are blessed as an individual, but we understood that the blessings of God are in Deuteronomy 28, and they refer to our condition as a nation of people. Our enemies fleeing from us is part of that blessing.

note.label: Psalm 68: Let God Arise

precepts.why:
“Let God arise, let his enemies be scattered: let them also that hate him flee before him.” This is going into the blessing again. Today people say they are blessed as an individual, but we understood that the blessings of God are in Deuteronomy 28, and they refer to our condition as a nation of people. “if thou shalt hearken diligently unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe and to do all his commandments which I command thee this day, that the Lord thy God will set thee on high above all nations of the earth: And all these blessings shall come on thee, and overtake thee”.

Among those blessings: “The Lord shall cause thine enemies that rise up against thee to be smitten before thy face: they shall come out against thee one way, and flee before thee seven ways.” Our enemies fleeing from us is part of that blessing. As smoke is driven away and wax melts before the fire, so the wicked perish at the presence of God, and they that hate him flee before him.

precepts.text: Disobedience brings the diseases of Egypt to cleave unto us, such as we suffer today.
precepts.point: He gave them the lands of the heathen and the labor of the people, that they might keep His statutes and laws. But we were not thankful, we went into idolatry, and now we are scattered in Babylon in America.

note.label: Psalm 105: Remember His Marvelous Works from Abraham to the Exodus

precepts.why:
“He brought them forth also with silver and gold: and there was not one feeble person among their tribes.” Not one feeble person coming out of Egypt. Look at the sicknesses we suffer now under the curses.

Deuteronomy tells why: “If thou wilt not observe to do all the words of this law that are written in this book, that thou mayest fear this glorious and fearful name, THE LORD THY GOD; Then the Lord will make thy plagues wonderful, and the plagues of thy seed, even great plagues, and of long continuance, and sore sicknesses, and of long continuance.”

“Moreover he will bring upon thee all the diseases of Egypt, which thou wast afraid of; and they shall cleave unto thee.” The very diseases of Egypt that Israel walked out from, whole and strong, come back and cleave to us through disobedience. That is the sickness we suffer today.

precepts.text: Because we served not the Most High with joyfulness for the good given us, these curses came; remember why we are here.
precepts.point: He gave them the lands of the heathen and the labor of the people, that they might keep His statutes and laws. But we were not thankful, we went into idolatry, and now we are scattered in Babylon in America.

note.label: Psalm 105: Remember His Marvelous Works from Abraham to the Exodus

precepts.why:
He gave them the lands of the heathen and the labour of the people, “That they might observe his statutes, and keep his laws.” Everything he did, the cloud for a covering, the fire for light, the quails, the bread of heaven and the water out of the rock, was done so that Israel would keep his laws.

But we were not thankful. “Because thou servedst not the Lord thy God with joyfulness, and with gladness of heart, for the abundance of all things”: that is why the curses came. We went into idolatry, and now we are scattered in Babylon in America.

Remember why we are here. He remembered his holy promise to Abraham and brought forth his people with joy; we did not serve him with joyfulness for the good given us.

precepts.text: The stranger shall rise high above us and we shall come down, brought low for our iniquity.
precepts.point: Nevertheless He regarded their affliction, remembered His covenant, and repented according to His mercies; David prays: save us and gather us from among the heathen. Blessed be the Lord God of Israel from everlasting to everlasting.

note.label: Psalm 106: Israel's Rebellions and the Mercy That Gathers Them Again

precepts.why:
“Their enemies also oppressed them, and they were brought into subjection under their hand.” Deuteronomy describes that subjection: “The stranger that is within thee shall get up above thee very high; and thou shalt come down very low. He shall lend to thee, and thou shalt not lend to him: he shall be the head, and thou shalt be the tail.”

The stranger rises very high above us and we come down very low, brought low for our iniquity, as the psalm says: “they provoked him with their counsel, and were brought low for their iniquity.” He delivered them many times, yet this is where their provoking landed them.

Nevertheless he regarded their affliction when he heard their cry and remembered for them his covenant. That is why David prays, “Save us, O Lord our God, and gather us from among the heathen”.

precepts.text: If you will not hearken unto the voice of the Lord to observe and do all His commandments, all these curses shall come upon you and overtake you, and this is why the curses came upon us as a people.
precepts.point: Because we rebelled and hated this Bible, He brought down our heart with labor, He brought down our minds with slavery. We fell down and there was none to help.

note.label: Psalm 107: O Give Thanks unto the Lord

precepts.why:
“Because they rebelled against the words of God, and contemned the counsel of the most High”. That rebellion is exactly what the curses of Deuteronomy 28 are for: “if thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes which I command thee this day; that all these curses shall come upon thee, and overtake thee”.

This is why the curses came upon us as a people. We would not hearken to observe and do all his commandments, so all these curses came upon us and overtook us, and we sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, bound in affliction and iron.

precepts.text: These curses are a sign and a wonder upon us and our seed forever, generational curses, because we served not the Lord with joyfulness and gladness of heart, so we serve our enemies in hunger, thirst, and nakedness with a yoke of iron.
precepts.point: Because we rebelled and hated this Bible, He brought down our heart with labor, He brought down our minds with slavery. We fell down and there was none to help.

note.label: Psalm 107: O Give Thanks unto the Lord

precepts.why:
“And they shall be upon thee for a sign and for a wonder, and upon thy seed for ever.” These curses are a sign and a wonder upon us and our seed forever: generational curses. That is why we are still bound in affliction and iron today, in captivity, even as we are raising back up and learning the words of God.

“Because thou servedst not the Lord thy God with joyfulness, and with gladness of heart, for the abundance of all things; Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies which the Lord shall send against thee, in hunger, and in thirst, and in nakedness, and in want of all things: and he shall put a yoke of iron upon thy neck, until he have destroyed thee.”

The “affliction and iron” of the psalm is this yoke of iron. Because we rebelled against the words of God and hated this Bible, he brought down our heart with labour and our minds with slavery, and we serve our enemies in hunger, thirst and nakedness.

precepts.text: The Lord brings us into Egypt again with ships, sold unto our enemies for bondmen and bondwomen, and no man buys us, identifying the children of Israel as the so-called blacks, Hispanics, and native Indians who went on the slave ships.
precepts.point: Because we rebelled and hated this Bible, He brought down our heart with labor, He brought down our minds with slavery. We fell down and there was none to help.

note.label: Psalm 107: O Give Thanks unto the Lord

precepts.why:
“And the Lord shall bring thee into Egypt again with ships, by the way whereof I spake unto thee, Thou shalt see it no more again: and there ye shall be sold unto your enemies for bondmen and bondwomen, and no man shall buy you.”

This is the captivity the psalm speaks of. The Lord brings us into Egypt again with ships, we are sold unto our enemies for bondmen and bondwomen, and no man buys us. It identifies the children of Israel as the so-called blacks, Hispanics and native Indians who went on the slave ships.

That is how we came to sit in darkness and in the shadow of death, bound in affliction and iron: we “fell down, and there was none to help.”

precepts.text: We grope at noonday as the blind grope in darkness, seeing the truth right in front of us but walking right on by, only oppressed and spoiled evermore with no man to save us.
precepts.point: Because we rebelled and hated this Bible, He brought down our heart with labor, He brought down our minds with slavery. We fell down and there was none to help.

note.label: Psalm 107: O Give Thanks unto the Lord

precepts.why:
“And thou shalt grope at noonday, as the blind gropeth in darkness, and thou shalt not prosper in thy ways: and thou shalt be only oppressed and spoiled evermore, and no man shall save thee.”

This is the darkness of the psalm. We grope at noonday as the blind grope in darkness, seeing the truth right in front of us but walking right on by. We are only oppressed and spoiled evermore, and “there was none to help”: no man to save us.

precepts.text: Because of these idols the Most High said He would scatter us among all people and there we would serve other gods of wood and stone.
precepts.point: Their idols are silver and gold, the work of men's hands. They have mouths but speak not, eyes but see not, ears but hear not, and they that make them are like unto them. This is going into idols and idolatry, which is spoken of throughout the scriptures.

note.label: Psalm 115: Not Unto Us, But Unto Thy Name Give Glory

precepts.why:
“And the Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other; and there thou shalt serve other gods, which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone.”

Because of these idols, the Most High said he would scatter us among all people and there we would serve other gods of wood and stone. That is the idolatry the psalm describes, spoken of throughout the scriptures, and it followed us into the scattering: idols with mouths that speak not and eyes that see not, and they that make them are like unto them.

precepts.text: The curses for disobedience that Solomon points to as the past the Most High requires, fulfilled on Israel.
precepts.point: That which has been is now, and the Most High requires that which is past. The sins of our past he requires, which is why Deuteronomy 28 had to come to pass, given to us in Deuteronomy and fulfilled upon us in the 1600s.

note.label: Ecclesiastes 3: A Time to Every Purpose

precepts.why:
“That which hath been is now; and that which is to be hath already been; and God requireth that which is past.” The sins of our past he requires. That is why Deuteronomy 28 had to come to pass: “if thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes which I command thee this day; that all these curses shall come upon thee, and overtake thee”.

The curses were given to us in Deuteronomy and fulfilled upon us in the 1600s. Whatever the Most High does shall be for ever; nothing can be put to it nor taken from it, and he does it that men should fear before him. The commandments were given forever, Israel was chosen forever, and Esau is hated forever; and the past the Most High requires overtook Israel exactly as it was written.

precepts.text: The curse: a nation swift as the eagle whose tongue thou shalt not understand, which is America and the white man, whose culture was repeated and beaten in.
precepts.point: With stammering lips and another tongue He will speak to this people; off the slave ships Israel spoke different languages, and because they did not keep the law the oppressor's culture was beaten into them until they came to understand. This Bible is the rest and the refreshing, yet they would not hear, so the word came precept upon precept that they might fall backward and be broken and snared.

note.label: Isaiah 28: Woe to the Drunkards of Ephraim and Precept Upon Precept

precepts.why:
The other tongue of Isaiah 28:11 is one of the curses of the law: “The Lord shall bring a nation against thee from far, from the end of the earth, as swift as the eagle flieth; a nation whose tongue thou shalt not understand”. That nation, swift as the eagle, is America and the white man, a nation whose tongue Israel did not understand.

This is how “with stammering lips and another tongue will he speak to this people” was fulfilled. Off the slave ships Israel spoke different languages, and because they did not keep the law, the oppressor’s culture was repeated and beaten into them until they came to understand. The Bible was “the rest wherewith ye may cause the weary to rest” and “the refreshing: yet they would not hear”, so the word came to them precept upon precept “that they might go, and fall backward, and be broken, and snared, and taken.”

precepts.text: Cursed in the city and cursed in the field, because of the high crime and black-on-black violence among us.
precepts.point: Blessed are they that sow beside all waters and send out the feet of the ox and the ass.

note.label: Isaiah 32: A King Shall Reign in Righteousness

precepts.why:
“And my people shall dwell in a peaceable habitation, and in sure dwellings, and in quiet resting places”. We are not dwelling peaceably now; we are under the curse: “Cursed shalt thou be in the city, and cursed shalt thou be in the field.”

Cursed in the city and cursed in the field, because of the high crime and black-on-black violence among us. There are no sure dwellings and quiet resting places in that. So we wait on that peace to return, when hail comes down on the forest, the city is brought low, and the Most High’s people dwell in a peaceable habitation.

precepts.text: The opening of the curses for breaking the laws, running from verse fifteen through sixty-eight, the punishments that came upon Israel.
precepts.point: Therefore I have profaned the princes of the sanctuary and given Jacob to the curse and Israel to reproaches. The Most High gave Jacob to the curse.

note.label: Isaiah 43: Ye Are My Witnesses

precepts.why:
“Therefore I have profaned the princes of the sanctuary, and have given Jacob to the curse”. The curse is written: “But it shall come to pass, if thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes which I command thee this day; that all these curses shall come upon thee, and overtake thee”.

This is the opening of the curses for breaking the laws, running from verse fifteen through sixty-eight, the punishments that came upon Israel. Israel did not hearken, did not bring the small cattle of the burnt offerings, made him to serve with their sins and wearied him with their iniquities, and thy first father hath sinned and thy teachers have transgressed, so all these curses came upon Jacob and overtook him. That is the curse the Most High gave Jacob to, and the reproaches he gave Israel to.

precepts.text: Thou shalt become an astonishment, a proverb, and a byword among all nations; our nationality and name were changed, called African American, one of the curses driven upon us.
precepts.point: This is prophecy of our name being changed back: on the sabbath classes a member is announced no longer a Corinthian or an Ephesian, because they take a pen and legalize their name change, subscribing with the hand as the scripture said.

note.label: Isaiah 44: The Idol Maker's Folly and the Changed Name

precepts.why:
Another shall “surname himself by the name of Israel.” Why does the name have to be taken back? Because of the curse: “And thou shalt become an astonishment, a proverb, and a byword, among all nations whither the Lord shall lead thee.”

Thou shalt become an astonishment, a proverb and a byword among all nations. Our nationality and name were changed, called African American, one of the curses driven upon us in the nations whither the Lord led us. Isaiah 44 is the prophecy of the name being changed back: one calling himself by the name of Jacob, another subscribing with his hand unto the Lord, which is why on the sabbath classes a member is announced no longer a Corinthian or an Ephesian, having taken a pen and legalized the name change.

precepts.text: The Lord shall scatter thee among all people, and there thou shalt serve other gods of wood and stone; two of the false religions we were cursed into serving are Christianity and Islam, gods our fathers never knew.
precepts.point: There is no God else beside me, a just God and a Saviour; look unto me and be ye saved, all the ends of the earth, for God scattered us to the ends of the earth. I have sworn by myself that unto me every knee shall bow and every tongue shall swear; in the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified and shall glory.

note.label: Isaiah 45: I Form the Light and Create Darkness

precepts.why:
“Look unto me, and be ye saved, all the ends of the earth: for I am God, and there is none else.” Why the ends of the earth? Because God scattered us there: “And the Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other; and there thou shalt serve other gods, which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone.”

The Lord scattered us among all people, from one end of the earth to the other, and there we serve other gods of wood and stone that our fathers never knew. Two of the false religions we were cursed into serving are Christianity and Islam, gods our fathers never knew. That is who is told, “Assemble yourselves and come; draw near together, ye that are escaped of the nations”, the ones with “no knowledge that set up the wood of their graven image, and pray unto a god that cannot save.” Come out from among them and be separate, touch not the unclean thing, and I will receive you: look unto him from the ends of the earth and be saved, for “In the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and shall glory.”

precepts.text: The Most High foretold He would bring a nation from the end of the earth, swift as an eagle, of fierce countenance and strange tongue, that regards neither old nor young.
precepts.point: He will bring a mighty and ancient nation from far, whose language they know not, upon the house of Israel.

note.label: Jeremiah 5: None That Executeth Judgment

precepts.why:
“The Lord shall bring a nation against thee from far, from the end of the earth, as swift as the eagle flieth; a nation whose tongue thou shalt not understand; A nation of fierce countenance, which shall not regard the person of the old, nor shew favour to the young”. The Most High foretold this long before Jeremiah: a nation from the end of the earth, swift as an eagle, of fierce countenance and strange tongue, that regards neither old nor young.

Jeremiah says the same thing to the house of Israel: “it is a mighty nation, it is an ancient nation, a nation whose language thou knowest not, neither understandest what they say.” Because they spoke against him, the Most High made his words in Jeremiah's mouth fire and this people wood, to devour them, and everything Jeremiah said came to pass.

precepts.text: All these curses come on those who will not obey the voice of the Lord.
precepts.point: Hear the words of this covenant: cursed be the man that obeys not its words.

note.label: Jeremiah 11: The Broken Covenant

precepts.why:
Here is what the curse on the man that obeys not looks like: “if thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes which I command thee this day; that all these curses shall come upon thee, and overtake thee”.

The words of the covenant are his commandments and his statutes. To not obey the voice of the Lord is to not observe to do them, and all these curses come on that man and overtake him. That is the curse Jeremiah is sent to remind Judah and Jerusalem of.

precepts.text: The curses came because we came in and possessed the land but would not walk in the ways of the Most High as He commanded.
precepts.point: The people came in and possessed the land but obeyed not His voice nor walked in His law, therefore He caused all this evil to come upon them, even as the mounts came up against the city to take it.

note.label: Jeremiah 32: Buying the Field of Redemption

precepts.why:
In his prayer Jeremiah confesses the whole matter: the Lord gave our fathers the land flowing with milk and honey, “And they came in, and possessed it; but they obeyed not thy voice, neither walked in thy law; they have done nothing of all that thou commandedst them to do: therefore thou hast caused all this evil to come upon them”.

That evil was the curse Moses had written: “if thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes which I command thee this day; that all these curses shall come upon thee, and overtake thee”. The curses came because we came in and possessed the land but would not walk in the ways of the Most High as he commanded. The mounts against the city, the sword, the famine and the pestilence, and the city given into the hand of the Chaldeans, are those curses overtaking us.

precepts.text: He would scatter us among all people from one end of the earth to the other.
precepts.point: He will give the men who transgressed His covenant, who cut the calf in twain and passed between the parts thereof, into the hand of their enemies.

note.label: Jeremiah 34: Liberty Proclaimed and Then Revoked

precepts.why:
The removal into all the kingdoms of the earth is the curse of the law: “And the Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other; and there thou shalt serve other gods, which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone.”

He would scatter us among all people from one end of the earth to the other. The men that transgressed his covenant, that cut the calf in twain and passed between the parts thereof and did not perform the words they made before him, are given over to that scattering, the same curse Moses wrote.

precepts.text: Our carcasses would be meat unto the fowls of the air and the beasts of the earth.
precepts.point: Zedekiah and his princes He will give into the hand of Babylon's army, which He will cause to return, take, and burn the city, and make the cities of Judah a desolation without inhabitant.

note.label: Jeremiah 34: Liberty Proclaimed and Then Revoked

precepts.why:
The princes, the eunuchs, the priests and all the people that passed between the parts of the calf are given into the hand of their enemies, “and their dead bodies shall be for meat unto the fowls of the heaven, and to the beasts of the earth.” That is the curse of the law word for word: “And thy carcase shall be meat unto all fowls of the air, and unto the beasts of the earth, and no man shall fray them away.”

Our carcasses would be meat unto the fowls of the air and the beasts of the earth. What Moses wrote as a curse for not keeping the covenant, Jeremiah announces on the men that broke it, with Zedekiah and his princes given into the hand of the king of Babylon's army.

precepts.text: All these curses of the law shall come upon them, pursue them, and overtake them until they are destroyed, even those who sought refuge in Egypt, because they hearkened not to the voice of the Most High.
precepts.point: They shall become an execration, an astonishment, a curse, and a reproach; only a small number escaping the sword shall return, for none shall return to Judah though they have a desire to dwell there.

note.label: Jeremiah 44: The Judgment on the Jews Who Fled to Egypt

precepts.why:
The remnant of Judah that set their faces to go into Egypt would be consumed by the sword and the famine, from the least to the greatest, and become an execration, an astonishment, a curse and a reproach. Moses had written that the curses follow: “Moreover all these curses shall come upon thee, and shall pursue thee, and overtake thee, till thou be destroyed; because thou hearkenedst not unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to keep his commandments and his statutes which he commanded thee”.

All these curses of the law come upon them, pursue them, and overtake them until they are destroyed, even those who sought refuge in Egypt. They were not humbled even to that day, nor did they fear or walk in his law and his statutes, so fleeing Jerusalem did not escape the curse; it pursued them into Egypt, and none returned to Judah but such as escaped.

precepts.text: These curses are a sign upon us and upon our seed forever because we served not the Most High with joyfulness and gladness of heart.
precepts.point: This should sound familiar; the same siege and famine came on us again under the Romans in 70 A.D. These are generational curses that fall on multiple generations when we break the Most High's commandments.

note.label: Jeremiah 52: The Fall of Jerusalem and the Puppet King Zedekiah

precepts.why:
“And they shall be upon thee for a sign and for a wonder, and upon thy seed for ever.” These curses are a sign upon us and upon our seed forever because we served not the Most High with joyfulness and gladness of heart.

That is why the siege of Jerusalem should sound familiar. Nebuchadnezzar and all his army pitched against the city and built forts round about it, and the famine was so sore “that there was no bread for the people of the land.” The same siege and famine came on us again under the Romans in 70 A.D. These are generational curses that fall on multiple generations when we break the Most High's commandments: upon thee, and upon thy seed for ever.

precepts.text: The Most High would bring a nation from far, swift as the eagle, of fierce countenance, to besiege the gates and destroy the food until the people ate the flesh of their own sons and daughters.
precepts.point: This should sound familiar; the same siege and famine came on us again under the Romans in 70 A.D. These are generational curses that fall on multiple generations when we break the Most High's commandments.

note.label: Jeremiah 52: The Fall of Jerusalem and the Puppet King Zedekiah

precepts.why:
The siege was written before it happened. “The Lord shall bring a nation against thee from far, from the end of the earth, as swift as the eagle flieth; a nation whose tongue thou shalt not understand; A nation of fierce countenance, which shall not regard the person of the old, nor shew favour to the young”.

That nation eats “the fruit of thy cattle, and the fruit of thy land, until thou be destroyed”, leaving neither corn, wine, nor oil. “And he shall besiege thee in all thy gates, until thy high and fenced walls come down, wherein thou trustedst, throughout all thy land”. The food is destroyed until “thou shalt eat the fruit of thine own body, the flesh of thy sons and of thy daughters, which the Lord thy God hath given thee, in the siege, and in the straitness, wherewith thine enemies shall distress thee”.

That is what Nebuchadnezzar and all his army did: they came against Jerusalem, pitched against it, built forts round about, and besieged it until the eleventh year of Zedekiah, until the famine was so sore there was no bread for the people of the land. And the same siege and famine came on us again under the Romans in 70 A.D.; these are generational curses that fall on multiple generations when we break the Most High's commandments.

precepts.text: The Most High would bring the people and their king into a nation neither they nor their fathers had known, to serve other gods of wood and stone.
precepts.point: Then they put out Zedekiah's eyes, so the last thing he would ever see was his sons put to death in his face, and they bound him in chains, carried him to Babylon, and kept him in prison till the day of his death; the Most High allowed these heathen to bring hell into Jerusalem.

note.label: Jeremiah 52: The Fall of Jerusalem and the Puppet King Zedekiah

precepts.why:
“The Lord shall bring thee, and thy king which thou shalt set over thee, unto a nation which neither thou nor thy fathers have known; and there shalt thou serve other gods, wood and stone.” The people and their king together, carried into a nation they had never known.

That is Zedekiah bound in chains and carried to Babylon, kept in prison till the day of his death, after the king of Babylon slew his sons before his eyes and put out his eyes. The Chaldeans overtook him in the plains of Jericho, his army scattered from him, and brought him up to Riblah in the land of Hamath for judgment. The Most High allowed these heathen to bring hell into Jerusalem, because he had said the king they set over themselves would go with them into that strange nation.

precepts.text: The Most High warned that a nation from far, whose tongue we understand not, would besiege us in all our gates, the curse that had to be inflicted once we went too far.
precepts.point: Because her filthiness is lewdness and He purged her yet she was not purged, she shall not be purged from her filthiness anymore until He has caused His fury to rest upon her. He will not go back, nor spare, nor repent; there is no more sackcloth or fasting to turn Him back at this point.

note.label: Ezekiel 24: The Boiling Pot and the Sign of the Prophet's Wife

precepts.why:
“Woe to the bloody city! I will even make the pile for fire great.” The Most High does not merely cook it and let the flame die; He stacks the wood and keeps it lit, “Heap on wood, kindle the fire, consume the flesh”, so we cook long and well, and then sets the pot empty on the coals till the brass is hot and the scum consumed.

Moses warned this was coming. “The Lord shall bring a nation against thee from far, from the end of the earth, as swift as the eagle flieth; a nation whose tongue thou shalt not understand; A nation of fierce countenance, which shall not regard the person of the old, nor shew favour to the young”. That nation eats the fruit of thy cattle and the fruit of thy land “until thou be destroyed”, and “shall besiege thee in all thy gates, until thy high and fenced walls come down, wherein thou trustedst”.

That is the curse that had to be inflicted once we went too far. “I have purged thee, and thou wast not purged”, so she “shalt not be purged from thy filthiness any more, till I have caused my fury to rest upon thee.” He will not go back, nor spare, nor repent; there is no more sackcloth or fasting to turn Him back at this point. The nation from far, whose tongue we understood not, besieging us in all our gates, is the fire under the pot.

precepts.text: The Most High shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other.
precepts.point: Our people were scattered everywhere because of our transgressions, exactly as the law warned.

note.label: Daniel 9: The Seventy Weeks

precepts.why:
“And the Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other; and there thou shalt serve other gods, which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone.” That is the law's warning, and Daniel's prayer is the warning fulfilled. Confusion of faces belongs “to the men of Judah, and to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and unto all Israel, that are near, and that are far off, through all the countries whither thou hast driven them, because of their trespass that they have trespassed against thee.”

Our people were scattered everywhere because of our transgressions, exactly as the law warned. Daniel lays it where it belongs, on us: “to our kings, to our princes, and to our fathers, because we have sinned against thee.” The scattering from one end of the earth to the other came because we rebelled: “Neither have we obeyed the voice of the Lord our God, to walk in his laws, which he set before us by his servants the prophets.”

And yet “To the Lord our God belong mercies and forgivenesses, though we have rebelled against him”. Righteousness is his, confusion of face is ours, and mercy is still his to give.

precepts.text: If thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the Most High to do his commandments, all these curses shall come upon thee and overtake thee.
precepts.point: The oath that was written is Deuteronomy 28, verses 1 through 68.

note.label: Daniel 9: The Seventy Weeks

precepts.why:
“But it shall come to pass, if thou wilt not hearken unto the voice of the Lord thy God, to observe to do all his commandments and his statutes which I command thee this day; that all these curses shall come upon thee, and overtake thee”. This is the oath Daniel is confessing: “the curse is poured upon us, and the oath that is written in the law of Moses the servant of God, because we have sinned against him.” The oath that was written is Deuteronomy 28, verses 1 through 68, and verse 15 is where the curses begin.

All Israel transgressed the law “even by departing, that they might not obey thy voice”. That is not hearkening to the voice of the Lord, and the curses came upon them and overtook them just as Moses wrote. The Lord “confirmed his words, which he spake against us” by bringing a great evil, “for under the whole heaven hath not been done as hath been done upon Jerusalem.”

Even so, “yet made we not our prayer before the Lord our God, that we might turn from our iniquities, and understand thy truth.” The Most High is righteous in all his works: the curse was written in the law before the evil came, and it came because “we obeyed not his voice.”

precepts.text: Thou shalt carry much seed into the field and gather but little in, for the locust shall consume it, which is exactly what Joel just read.
precepts.point: This came upon Israel during the time going into the Babylonian captivity, when they still had their own land, crops, and vineyards, and had to endure the curses of Deuteronomy 28. These are curses you do not usually hear brought out on the street, because they fell on us when we actually had our own land.

note.label: Joel 1: The Palmerworm, the Locust, and the Lion Out of the North

precepts.why:
“That which the palmerworm hath left hath the locust eaten”. This is the plague coming on the crops through the locusts and cankerworms, and it is a curse: “Thou shalt carry much seed out into the field, and shalt gather but little in; for the locust shall consume it.” That is exactly what Joel just read.

This came upon Israel during the time going into the Babylonian captivity, when they still had their own land, crops, and vineyards, and had to endure the curses of Deuteronomy 28. These are curses you do not usually hear brought out on the street, because they fell on us when we actually had our own land.

precepts.text: Thou shalt plant vineyards and dress them but neither drink of the wine nor gather the grapes, for the worms shall eat them.
precepts.point: This came upon Israel during the time going into the Babylonian captivity, when they still had their own land, crops, and vineyards, and had to endure the curses of Deuteronomy 28. These are curses you do not usually hear brought out on the street, because they fell on us when we actually had our own land.

note.label: Joel 1: The Palmerworm, the Locust, and the Lion Out of the North

precepts.why:
The curse keeps going, the way Joel's plague does: “Thou shalt plant vineyards, and dress them, but shalt neither drink of the wine, nor gather the grapes; for the worms shall eat them.” What the locust left the cankerworm eats, and what the cankerworm left the caterpiller eats, right down to the vineyards.

This fell on Israel going into the Babylonian captivity, when they still had their own land, crops, and vineyards to plant and dress. You do not usually hear these curses brought out on the street, because they fell on us when we actually had our own land.

precepts.text: Thou shalt build a house and not dwell therein, and plant a vineyard and not gather the grapes; the same curse first pronounced in Deuteronomy.
precepts.point: Forasmuch as their treading is upon the poor and they take from him burdens of wheat, they have built houses of hewn stone but shall not dwell in them, and planted pleasant vineyards but shall not drink the wine of them. These curses are generational from each captivity, the same thing repeating over and over.

note.label: Amos 5: Seek Ye Me and Ye Shall Live

precepts.why:
“ye have built houses of hewn stone, but ye shall not dwell in them; ye have planted pleasant vineyards, but ye shall not drink wine of them.” This is the same curse first pronounced in Deuteronomy: “thou shalt build an house, and thou shalt not dwell therein: thou shalt plant a vineyard, and shalt not gather the grapes thereof.”

These curses are generational from each captivity, the same thing repeating over and over. Because their treading is upon the poor and they take from him burdens of wheat, and because they hate him that rebukes in the gate and abhor him that speaks uprightly, which they do the same today, the curse of Deuteronomy falls on them again.

precepts.text: Thou shalt become an astonishment, a proverb, and a byword, among all nations whither the Lord shall lead thee.
precepts.point: There is nowhere in the scriptures where the Most High says he will save another nation to give them the kingdom. Israel is the one who needs a saviour, and the condition we are in is why.

note.label: Zechariah 8: I Will Return Unto Zion and Dwell in the Midst of Jerusalem

precepts.why:
As ye were a curse among the heathen, O house of Judah, and house of Israel. Both houses are named, the southern kingdom and the northern kingdom, and the curse among the heathen is the curse written in the law. “And thou shalt become an astonishment, a proverb, and a byword, among all nations whither the Lord shall lead thee.”

That is the condition we are in among the nations, and it is why Israel is the one who needs a saviour. The blessing he promises is the same blessing promised in that law for keeping the commandments.

precepts.text: The nation from far, the siege in all thy gates, and the eating of the fruit of thine own body.
precepts.point: Woe to them that are with child and to them that give suck in those days, and pray that your flight be not in the winter. What that siege was is written in the law.

note.label: Mark 13: The Signs of the End and the Charge to Watch

precepts.why:
“woe to them that are with child, and to them that give suck in those days! And pray ye that your flight be not in the winter.” What that siege was is written in the law.

“The Lord shall bring a nation against thee from far, from the end of the earth, as swift as the eagle flieth; a nation whose tongue thou shalt not understand; A nation of fierce countenance, which shall not regard the person of the old, nor shew favour to the young”. That nation eats the fruit of the cattle and the fruit of the land “until thou be destroyed”.

“And he shall besiege thee in all thy gates, until thy high and fenced walls come down, wherein thou trustedst, throughout all thy land”. That is Jerusalem compassed with armies. And in that siege: “thou shalt eat the fruit of thine own body, the flesh of thy sons and of thy daughters, which the Lord thy God hath given thee, in the siege, and in the straitness, wherewith thine enemies shall distress thee”.

That is why it is woe to them that are with child and to them that give suck in those days. The nation from far, the siege in all thy gates and the eating of the fruit of thine own body were written by Moses long before, and Christ tells them that day is coming on Judaea, so flee.

precepts.text: The Most High would bring a nation from far whose tongue thou shalt not understand, which is why Israel had to be taught in the captors' languages.
precepts.point: Because Israel was scattered among nations whose tongue they did not understand, the Most High spoke to his people with stammering lips and another tongue. The cloven tongues were the many languages of the lands where Israel was dispersed, and they spoke the word of the Most High in them like fire.

note.label: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

precepts.why:
The curse tells why other tongues were needed: “The Lord shall bring a nation against thee from far, from the end of the earth, as swift as the eagle flieth; a nation whose tongue thou shalt not understand”. Israel would be put under nations whose language they did not know.

Scattered among those nations, Israel took on the speech of their captors, so they had to be taught in the captors' languages. The cloven tongues that sat on the apostles were those languages, divided out so the word of the Most High could reach his people wherever they had been carried.

precepts.text: Thou shalt be removed into all the kingdoms of the earth, the source verse from which the word diaspora comes.
precepts.point: The historical record in A Tribute to the Negro says the Jews, though their features assimilated to the nations among whom they were scattered, descended from one stock, were forbidden to intermarry, and yet according to the divine prediction were dispersed into every country, marked with the colors of all: brown and swarthy in Turkey and Portugal, black in Spain, Syria, Chaldea, Arabia, Egypt, and at the Congo in Africa. Swarthy means dark and black, tawny means copper or brown, and olive is not "all colors," for a man of all colors would be a diseased spectacle, not a real man; Christ was black and brown.

note.label: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

precepts.why:
“The Lord shall cause thee to be smitten before thine enemies: thou shalt go out one way against them, and flee seven ways before them: and shalt be removed into all the kingdoms of the earth.” This is the source verse of the word diaspora. The word itself originated in the Septuagint at Deuteronomy 28:25, and the dictionaries define diaspora as the dispersion of the Jewish people beyond Israel.

There is no African diaspora that exists apart from this. The so-called African diaspora is the Israelite diaspora, because only Israel was scattered to all the earth by biblical prophecy. That is why Jews out of every nation under heaven were dwelling at Jerusalem.

precepts.text: The Most High shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other.
precepts.point: The historical record in A Tribute to the Negro says the Jews, though their features assimilated to the nations among whom they were scattered, descended from one stock, were forbidden to intermarry, and yet according to the divine prediction were dispersed into every country, marked with the colors of all: brown and swarthy in Turkey and Portugal, black in Spain, Syria, Chaldea, Arabia, Egypt, and at the Congo in Africa. Swarthy means dark and black, tawny means copper or brown, and olive is not "all colors," for a man of all colors would be a diseased spectacle, not a real man; Christ was black and brown.

note.label: Acts 2: Pentecost and the Scattered House of Israel

precepts.why:
“And the Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other”. From one end of the earth to the other is every nation under heaven, and that is where the devout men at Jerusalem had come from.

The historical record in A Tribute to the Negro bears it out. The Jews, though their features assimilated to the nations among whom they were scattered, descended from one stock and were forbidden to intermarry, and yet according to the divine prediction they were dispersed into every country, marked with the colors of all: brown and swarthy in Turkey and Portugal, black in Spain, Syria, Chaldea, Arabia, Egypt, and at the Congo in Africa. This verse is that divine prediction.

Swarthy means dark and black, and tawny means copper or brown. Olive is not all colors; a man of all colors would be a diseased spectacle, not a real man. Christ was black and brown.

precepts.text: Israel would be smitten before their enemies and "removed into all the kingdoms of the earth," the same scattered families of the earth that are to be blessed.
precepts.point: "Ye are the children of the prophets, and of the covenant which God made with our fathers, saying unto Abraham, And in thy seed shall all the kindreds of the earth be blessed." The "ye" are the children of Israel, and "kindreds" means a lineage or family that descends from a common progenitor, Abraham, not all nations.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

precepts.why:
How did the family spread abroad to the west, east, north and south? “The Lord shall cause thee to be smitten before thine enemies: thou shalt go out one way against them, and flee seven ways before them: and shalt be removed into all the kingdoms of the earth.”

Israel was removed into all the kingdoms of the earth. Those are the scattered families of the earth that are to be blessed in Abraham's seed: the one kindred, dispersed everywhere, not every nation.

precepts.text: Ye shall be scattered among the nations to serve gods of wood and stone, which is why our people were placed under these nations and indoctrinated.
precepts.point: Peter, Paul, John, and Christ all went to the rulers and builders of the people, not to the white church, the mosque, or the temple of Zeus. Our job is to go to the scribes, Sadducees, Pharisees, and religious leaders of our own captivity to reason and win some, not to the same people who raped, robbed, drugged, and miseducated us and would never give up their power. This is why bishop gave the order to go to these Christian pastors.

note.label: Acts 4: The Stone the Builders Rejected

precepts.why:
Peter answered the rulers of the people and elders of Israel; the conversation is still to Israel, always the Israelites. Why our people are where they are: “And the Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other; and there thou shalt serve other gods, which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone.”

That is why our people were placed under these nations and indoctrinated. Peter, Paul, John and Christ all went to the rulers and builders of the people, not to the white church, the mosque or the temple of Zeus. Our job is to go to the scribes, Sadducees, Pharisees and religious leaders of our own captivity to reason and win some, not to the same people who raped, robbed, drugged and miseducated us and would never give up their power. This is why bishop gave the order to go to these Christian pastors.

precepts.text: Scattered from one end of the earth to the other, serving other gods of wood and stone, part of the curse for disobedience.
precepts.point: "But in every nation he that feareth him and worketh righteousness is accepted with him." The "every nation" is not the Chinese, Japanese, East Indian, or Caucasian; it is every nation into which the Israelites were scattered for disobedience.

note.label: Acts 11: The Gentiles Are Scattered Israel

precepts.why:
“And the Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other; and there thou shalt serve other gods, which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone.”

The scattering is part of the curse for disobedience. Israel was scattered from one end of the earth to the other and served other gods of wood and stone. That is how Israel came to be in every nation, and how they came to be called Gentiles.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 6 The 4 Horsemen

precepts.why: The Chaldeans of Habakkuk 1 are a metaphor for the conquering of the Americas, because of what Deuteronomy 28:46 says. “And they shall be upon thee for a sign and for a wonder, and upon thy seed for ever.” So the curses of Israel, going into captivity, being conquered, would constantly happen.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 6 The 4 Horsemen

precepts.why:
“The stranger that is within thee” First of all he is an alien; the alien comes among us. Within thee means he came into your space. “shall get up above thee very high;” So he came into our house and got above us in our house. “and thou shalt come down very low.” In your own house you shall come very low.

“He shall lend to thee,” He lends money to us, in our house, with our resources, with our wood, our water; our water is sold unto us, our wood is sold unto us, in our house. Foreign policy guarantees this. “and thou shalt not lend to him:” We can't lend to him, even though it is your house, your resources, your bauxite, your gold, your diamonds; you ain't setting none of that. “he shall be the head,” He shall be the head nation, “and thou shalt be the tail.” We are the tail.

The End of Poverty shows an example of that. When the settlers moved from Kenya in 1964-65 up to 1970 they benchmarked their operations in Europe, so Africa became the producers of raw materials and they were the agents for marketing and processing; all the value addition of the crops was done away from Africa. Coffee and tea: Germany, which does not have a single bush of coffee, is the largest exporter of coffee. They are the devil the Bible speaks of. They took the coffee, paid the people pennies on a bushel to pick it, processed it, and now you have Starbucks at five dollars a damn cup. The tea you consume in Sudan goes first to Europe, then Lipton brings it back to Sudan. One of the legacies of colonialism is that the poor countries of the third world continue to export raw materials while Europe and North America export finished products; this stems from a practice developed long ago, with the intention that the third world remain backward and dependent and never able to develop, and it gets worse each year. They do that to make sure these nations can never rise above the poverty level. In Africa Esau only allows twelve countries to manufacture small weapons; the rest, you are not allowed, and if you do, we cut you off from the world and you die in poverty. Remember what the Clintons did to Haiti with the rice: bread, oil and rice are the things people use every day, and destroying them makes a country fall into deep poverty, so now you have to buy from them. In Sierra Leone something like 60% were illiterate: when you are poor, your kids can't go to school, because not only do they have to pay to go, they have to go out and work to bring a little bit of money to the house. From colonial times to this day.

note.label: Bishop Nathanyel | Revelation 11 A Time Of Defamation

precepts.why: The two witnesses had power, then the beast rose up and overcame them and killed them, and their dead bodies lie in the street of the great city. How did they get to the great city, for those that lived on the Eastern Hemisphere? Precept must be upon precept. The northern kingdom was already on this side, pretty much. “And the Lord shall bring thee into Egypt again with ships” That is how they got to the great city: with ships. And it is spiritually called Egypt. “by the way whereof I spake unto thee, Thou shalt see it no more again: and there ye shall be sold unto your enemies for bondmen and bondwomen, and no man shall buy you.” No man shall save us.

note.label: Spiritual Uprising: When God Shakes a Nation

precepts.why:
“And I will set my face against you”. God set his face against us. “and ye shall be slain before your enemies”. We're going to be killed before our enemies. “they that hate you shall reign over you”. Those who hate you are going to rule you. Who rules us today? Esau. Christians on social media talk as if Donald Trump and the white man are supposed to love us.
